title.zh: 卷二十四 志第十四 車服
title.raw: 卷二十四 志第十四 車服 Volume 24 Treatises 15: Carraiges and Attire

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 唐初受命，車、服皆因隋舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang's receiving the mandate, carriages and dress all followed Sui precedents.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang first received the Mandate, its carriage and attire regulations followed those of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，始著車輿、衣服之令，上得兼下，下不得儗上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, regulations for carriages and clothing were first promulgated: those above may encompass those below, but those below may not imitate those above.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4 (621), edicts on carriages and dress were issued under the rule that superiors might use insignia of lower ranks, but inferiors might not emulate those above.

sentences.zh: 凡天子之車：

translations.literal: As for the Son of Heaven's carriages:
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's carriages were as follows:

sentences.zh: 曰玉路者，祭祀、納后所乘也，青質，玉飾末；

translations.literal: That called the Jade Chariot was ridden for sacrifice and receiving the empress, with a green body and jade ornament on the tip.
translations.idiomatic: The Jade Chariot was used for sacrifices and for receiving an empress; its body was green, with jade ornament at the pole tip.

sentences.zh: 金路者，饗、射、祀還、飲至所乘也，赤質，金飾末；

translations.literal: The Golden Chariot was ridden for banquets, archery, return from sacrifice, and the "drink to arrival" rite, with a red body and gold ornament on the tip.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Chariot served banquets, archery, return from sacrifice, and victory feasts; its body was red, with gold ornament at the pole tip.

sentences.zh: 象路者，行道所乘也，黃質，象飾末；

translations.literal: The Ivory Chariot was ridden for traveling on the roads, with a yellow body and ivory ornament on the tip.
translations.idiomatic: The Ivory Chariot was used for ordinary progress on the roads; its body was yellow, with ivory ornament at the pole tip.

sentences.zh: 革路者，臨兵、巡守所乘也，白質，鞔以革；

translations.literal: The Leather Chariot was ridden for facing troops and patrol inspection, with a white body, covered in leather.
translations.idiomatic: The Leather Chariot was used when confronting armies or on inspection tours; its body was white and covered in leather.

sentences.zh: 木路者，蒐田所乘也，黑質，漆之。

translations.literal: The Wooden Chariot was ridden for the hunt, with a black body, lacquered.
translations.idiomatic: The Wooden Chariot was used for the imperial hunt; its body was black and lacquered.

sentences.zh: 五路皆重輿，左青龍，右白虎，金鳳翅，畫苣文鳥獸，黃屋左纛。

translations.literal: All five chariots had double carriages, azure dragon on the left and white tiger on the right, golden phoenix wings, painted with grain patterns, birds, and beasts, yellow canopy with left great banner.
translations.idiomatic: All five chariots had double bodies, an azure dragon on the left and a white tiger on the right, golden phoenix wings, grain-pattern and bird-and-beast painting, and a yellow canopy with the great banner on the left.

sentences.zh: 金鳳一、鈴二在軾前，鸞十二在衡，龍輈前設鄣塵。

translations.literal: One golden phoenix and two bells before the railing, twelve bells on the crossbar, dragon shafts with dust screen set before them.
translations.idiomatic: One golden phoenix and two bells were mounted before the railing; twelve phoenix bells hung on the crossbar; dragon shafts bore a dust screen ahead.

sentences.zh: 青蓋三層，繡飾。

translations.literal: Azure canopy of three layers, embroidered ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Its canopy had three azure layers with embroidered ornament.

sentences.zh: 上設博山方鏡，下圓鏡。

translations.literal: Above were set a Bo Mountain square mirror and a round mirror below.
translations.idiomatic: Above the canopy stood a square Bo Mountain mirror and, below it, a round mirror.

sentences.zh: 樹羽。

translations.literal: Feathered plumes were planted.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered plumes were set upon it.

sentences.zh: 輪金根、朱班、重牙。

translations.literal: Wheels with golden hubs, vermilion rim bands, and double teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The wheels had golden hubs, vermilion rim bands, and double teeth.

sentences.zh: 左建旂，十有二旒，畫升龍，其長曳地，青繡綢杠。

translations.literal: On the left a banner was erected with twelve tassels, painted with ascending dragons, its length trailing the ground, with an azure embroidered silk pole.
translations.idiomatic: On the left stood a banner of twelve tassels painted with ascending dragons, trailing to the ground, on an azure embroidered silk pole.

sentences.zh: 右載闟戟，長四尺，廣三尺，黻文。

translations.literal: On the right was carried a ge halberd four chi long and three chi wide, with fu pattern.
translations.idiomatic: On the right was carried a fu-patterned ge halberd four chi long and three chi wide.

sentences.zh: 旂首金龍銜錦結綬及緌帶，垂鈴。

translations.literal: The banner head had a golden dragon holding brocade knotted cords and sash ends, with hanging bells.
translations.idiomatic: The banner head bore a golden dragon clutching brocade knotted cords and sash ends, with bells hanging below.

sentences.zh: 金鍐方釳，插翟尾五焦，鏤鍚，鞶纓十二就。

translations.literal: Golden wei square yi, inserting five tufts of pheasant tail, carved yang, pan-ying in twelve sets.
translations.idiomatic: Golden wei square yi ornaments bore five tufts of pheasant tail, carved yang fittings, and pan-ying harness in twelve sets.

sentences.zh: 旌旗、蓋、鞶纓，皆從路質，唯蓋裏皆用黃。

translations.literal: Banners, canopy, and pan-ying all followed the chariot's material color; only the canopy lining was always yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Banners, canopy, and pan-ying all matched the chariot's base color; only the canopy lining was always yellow.

sentences.zh: 五路皆有副。

translations.literal: Each of the five chariots had a spare.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five chariots had a reserve duplicate.

sentences.zh: 耕根車者，耕藉所乘也，青質，三重蓋，餘如玉路。

translations.literal: The Plough-Root Chariot was ridden for ploughing the sacred field, with green body, triple canopy, the rest like the Jade Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The Plough-Root Chariot was used for ploughing the sacred field; it had a green body and triple canopy, otherwise matching the Jade Chariot.

sentences.zh: 安車者，臨幸所乘也，金飾重輿，曲壁，紫油纁，朱裏通幰，朱絲絡網，朱鞶纓，朱覆髮具絡，駕赤騮。

translations.literal: The Sedan Chariot was ridden on imperial visits, with gold ornament and double carriage, curved walls, purple oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, vermilion silk net, vermilion pan-ying, vermilion cap and hair-net fittings, drawn by chestnut bays.
translations.idiomatic: The Sedan Chariot was used on imperial visits: gold ornament, double body, curved walls, purple oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, vermilion silk net and pan-ying, vermilion cap and hair-net fittings, drawn by chestnut bays.

sentences.zh: 副路、耕根車、安車，皆八鸞。

translations.literal: Spare chariots, Plough-Root Chariot, and Sedan Chariot all had eight phoenix bells.
translations.idiomatic: Spare chariots, the Plough-Root Chariot, and the Sedan Chariot each carried eight phoenix bells.

sentences.zh: 四望車者，拜陵、臨弔所乘也，制如安車，青油纁，朱裏通幰，朱絲絡網。

translations.literal: The Four-View Chariot was ridden for worship at tombs and condolence visits, made like the Sedan Chariot, with green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, vermilion silk net.
translations.idiomatic: The Four-View Chariot was used for tomb worship and condolence calls; like the Sedan Chariot, it had a green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, and vermilion silk net.

sentences.zh: 又有屬車十乘：一曰指南車，二曰記里鼓車，三曰白鷺車，四曰鸞旗車，五曰辟惡車，六曰皮軒車，七曰羊車，與耕根車、四望車、安車為十乘。

translations.literal: There were also ten attendant chariots: first the south-pointing chariot, second the odometer drum chariot, third the egret chariot, fourth the phoenix-banner chariot, fifth the demon-warding chariot, sixth the tiger-skin canopy chariot, seventh the goat chariot — together with the Plough-Root, Four-View, and Sedan chariots making ten.
translations.idiomatic: There were also ten attendant chariots: the south-pointing chariot, the odometer drum chariot, the egret chariot, the phoenix-banner chariot, the demon-warding chariot, the tiger-skin canopy chariot, and the goat chariot — with the Plough-Root, Four-View, and Sedan chariots, ten in all.

sentences.zh: 行幸陳於鹵簿，則分前後；

translations.literal: On progress they were arrayed in the guard of honor, then divided front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, they were drawn up in the guard of honor and divided into front and rear sections.

sentences.zh: 大朝會，則分左右。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies they were divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies they were arrayed to left and right.

sentences.zh: 皇后之車六：

translations.literal: The empress had six chariots:
translations.idiomatic: The empress had six chariots:

sentences.zh: 重翟車者，受冊、從祀、饗廟所乘也，青質，青油纁，朱裏通幰，繡紫絡帶及帷，八鸞，鏤鍚，鞶纓十二就，金鍐方釳，樹翟羽，朱總。

translations.literal: The Heavy Pheasant Chariot was ridden for receiving investiture, following sacrifice, and feasting at the temple, with green body, green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, embroidered purple net bands and curtains, eight phoenix bells, carved yang, pan-ying in twelve sets, golden wei square yi, pheasant plumes planted, vermilion tassels.
translations.idiomatic: The Heavy Pheasant Chariot was used when receiving investiture, following sacrifice, or feasting at the ancestral temple: green body, green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, embroidered purple net bands and curtains, eight phoenix bells, carved yang, twelve-set pan-ying, golden wei square yi, planted pheasant plumes, and vermilion tassels.

sentences.zh: 厭翟車者，親桑所乘也，赤質，紫油纁，朱裏通幰，紅錦絡帶及帷。

translations.literal: The Pressed Pheasant Chariot was ridden for personally tending the mulberry, with red body, purple oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, red brocade net bands and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The Pressed Pheasant Chariot was used when the empress personally tended the mulberry grove: red body, purple oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, red brocade net bands and curtains.

sentences.zh: 翟車者，歸寧所乘也，黃油纁，黃裏通幰，白紅錦絡帶及帷。

translations.literal: The Pheasant Chariot was ridden for returning to her parents' home, with yellow oil canopy, yellow lining and full screen, white and red brocade net bands and curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The Pheasant Chariot was used when returning to her parents' home: yellow oil canopy, yellow lining and full screen, white and red brocade net bands and curtains.

sentences.zh: 三車皆金飾末，輪畫朱牙，箱飾翟羽，朱絲絡網，鞶纓色皆從車質。

translations.literal: All three chariots had gold ornament on the tip, wheels painted with vermilion teeth, boxes ornamented with pheasant plumes, vermilion silk net, pan-ying colors all following the chariot's material.
translations.idiomatic: All three had gold pole tips, wheels painted with vermilion teeth, boxes ornamented with pheasant plumes, vermilion silk net, and pan-ying colors matching each chariot's base hue.

sentences.zh: 安車者，臨幸所乘也，制如金路，紫油纁，朱裏通幰。

translations.literal: The Sedan Chariot was ridden on visits, made like the Golden Chariot, with purple oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.
translations.idiomatic: The Sedan Chariot was used on visits, built like the Golden Chariot, with purple oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.

sentences.zh: 四望車者，拜陵、弔喪所乘也，青油纁，朱裏通幰。

translations.literal: The Four-View Chariot was ridden for tomb worship and mourning calls, with green oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.
translations.idiomatic: The Four-View Chariot was used for tomb worship and mourning calls, with green oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.

sentences.zh: 金根車者，常行所乘也，紫油纁，朱裏通幰。

translations.literal: The Golden-Root Chariot was ridden for ordinary travel, with purple oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden-Root Chariot was used for everyday travel, with purple oil canopy and vermilion lining and full screen.

sentences.zh: 夫人乘厭翟車，九嬪乘翟車，婕妤以下乘安車。

translations.literal: The consort rode the Pressed Pheasant Chariot, the nine concubines the Pheasant Chariot, and ladies below the Jieyu rank the Sedan Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The consort rode the Pressed Pheasant Chariot, the nine concubines the Pheasant Chariot, and ladies below Jieyu rank the Sedan Chariot.

sentences.zh: 外命婦、公主、王妃乘厭翟車。

translations.literal: Wives of officials with outside titles, princesses, and imperial sons' consorts rode the Pressed Pheasant Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Wives holding outside titles, princesses, and imperial sons' consorts rode the Pressed Pheasant Chariot.

sentences.zh: 一品乘白銅飾犢車，青油纁，朱裏通幰，朱絲絡網。

translations.literal: First rank rode a calf cart with white bronze ornament, green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, vermilion silk net.
translations.idiomatic: First rank rode a calf cart with white bronze fittings, green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, and vermilion silk net.

sentences.zh: 二品以下去油纁、絡網。

translations.literal: Second rank and below omitted the oil canopy and net.
translations.idiomatic: Second rank and below went without the oil canopy and silk net.

sentences.zh: 四品有青偏幰。

translations.literal: Fourth rank had an azure partial screen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank had an azure partial screen.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之車三：

translations.literal: The heir apparent had three chariots:
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had three chariots:

sentences.zh: 金路者，從祀、朝賀、納妃所乘也，赤質，金飾末，重較，箱畫苣文鳥獸，黃屋，伏鹿軾，龍輈，金鳳一，在軾前，設鄣塵，朱黃蓋裏，輪畫朱牙。

translations.literal: The Golden Chariot was ridden for following sacrifice, court congratulations, and receiving a consort, with red body, gold ornament on the tip, double rails, box painted with grain patterns, birds, and beasts, yellow canopy, crouching deer railing, dragon shafts, one golden phoenix before the railing, dust screen set, vermilion and yellow canopy lining, wheels painted with vermilion teeth.
translations.idiomatic: The Golden Chariot was used when following sacrifice, attending congratulatory court, or receiving a consort: red body, gold pole tip, double rails, box painted with grain patterns and birds and beasts, yellow canopy, crouching-deer railing, dragon shafts, one golden phoenix before the railing, dust screen, vermilion-and-yellow canopy lining, wheels with vermilion teeth.

sentences.zh: 左建旂九旒，右載闟戟，旂首金龍銜結綬及鈴緌，八鸞二鈴，金鍐方釳，樹翟尾五焦，鏤鍚，鞶纓九就。

translations.literal: On the left a banner of nine tassels was erected; on the right a ge halberd was carried; the banner head had a golden dragon holding knotted cords and bell sashes; eight phoenix bells and two bells; golden wei square yi; five tufts of pheasant tail planted; carved yang; pan-ying in nine sets.
translations.idiomatic: On the left stood a nine-tassel banner; on the right a ge halberd; the banner head bore a golden dragon with knotted cords and bell sashes; eight phoenix bells and two bells; golden wei square yi; five tufts of pheasant tail; carved yang; pan-ying in nine sets.

sentences.zh: 軺車者，五日常服、朝饗、宮臣、出入行道所乘也。

translations.literal: The light cart was ridden for daily dress on the five days, morning banquets, palace officials, and going out on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The light cart served everyday dress on the five ritual days, morning banquets, palace officials, and travel on the roads.

sentences.zh: 四望車者，臨弔所乘也。

translations.literal: The Four-View Chariot was ridden for condolence visits.
translations.idiomatic: The Four-View Chariot was used for condolence visits.

sentences.zh: 二車皆金飾末，紫油纁，朱裏通幰。

translations.literal: Both chariots had gold ornament on the tip, purple oil canopy, and vermilion lining and full screen.
translations.idiomatic: Both had gold pole tips, purple oil canopy, and vermilion lining and full screen.

sentences.zh: 親王及武職，一品有象路，青油纁，朱裏通幰，朱絲絡網。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and military offices of first rank had the Ivory Chariot, with green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, vermilion silk net.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and first-rank military posts used the Ivory Chariot, with green oil canopy, vermilion lining and full screen, and vermilion silk net.

sentences.zh: 二品、三品有革路，朱裏青通幰。

translations.literal: Second and third rank had the Leather Chariot, with vermilion lining and azure full screen.
translations.idiomatic: Second and third rank used the Leather Chariot, with vermilion lining and azure full screen.

sentences.zh: 四品有木路，五品有軺車，皆碧裏青偏幰。

translations.literal: Fourth rank had the Wooden Chariot, fifth rank the light cart, all with green lining and azure partial screen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth rank had the Wooden Chariot, fifth rank the light cart, each with green lining and azure partial screen.

sentences.zh: 象飾末，班輪，八鸞，左建旂，畫升龍，右載闟戟。

translations.literal: Ivory ornament on the tip, rim bands on the wheels, eight phoenix bells, banner erected on the left painted with ascending dragon, ge halberd carried on the right.
translations.idiomatic: They bore ivory pole tips, rimmed wheels, eight phoenix bells, a left banner painted with ascending dragons, and a ge halberd on the right.

sentences.zh: 革路、木路，左建旜。

translations.literal: Leather and Wooden chariots had a pennant erected on the left.
translations.idiomatic: Leather and Wooden chariots bore a pennant on the left.

sentences.zh: 軺車，曲壁，碧裏青通幰。

translations.literal: The light cart had curved walls, green lining and azure full screen.
translations.idiomatic: The light cart had curved walls, green lining, and azure full screen.

sentences.zh: 諸路，朱質、朱蓋、朱旂、朱班輪。

translations.literal: All chariots had vermilion body, vermilion canopy, vermilion banners, and vermilion rim bands on the wheels.
translations.idiomatic: All such chariots had vermilion body, canopy, banners, and rim bands.

sentences.zh: 一品之旜九旒，二品八旒，三品七旒，四品六旒，鞶纓就亦如之。

translations.literal: First rank's pennant had nine tassels, second eight, third seven, fourth six; pan-ying sets likewise.
translations.idiomatic: First rank bore nine pennant tassels, second eight, third seven, fourth six; pan-ying sets followed the same scale.

sentences.zh: 三品以上珂九子，四品七子，五品五子，六品以下去通幰及珂。

translations.literal: Third rank and above had nine ke ornaments, fourth seven, fifth five; sixth rank and below omitted full screen and ke.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above had nine ke ornaments, fourth seven, fifth five; sixth rank and below went without full screen and ke.

sentences.zh: 王公車路，藏於太僕，受制、行冊命、巡陵、昏葬則給之。

translations.literal: Princes' and dukes' chariots were stored in the Imperial Stud; they were issued on receiving orders, promulgating investiture, touring tombs, or weddings and funerals.
translations.idiomatic: Princes' and dukes' chariots were kept in the Imperial Stud and issued only when receiving orders, promulgating investiture, touring tombs, or for weddings and funerals.

sentences.zh: 餘皆以騎代車。

translations.literal: For the rest, riding replaced the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: On other occasions they rode horseback instead.

sentences.zh: 凡天子之服十四：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had fourteen sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven had fourteen sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 大裘冕者，祀天地之服也。

translations.literal: The Great Fur and Miǎn Crown was dress for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Fur Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn when sacrificing to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 廣八寸，長一尺二寸，以板為之，黑表，纁裏，無旒，金飾玉簪導，組帶為纓，色如其綬，黈纊充耳。

translations.literal: Eight cun wide and one chi two cun long, made of board, black outside and xuan lining, no tassels, gold ornament and jade hairpin guide, group cords for the chin strap, color like the sash, huang yarn filling the ears.
translations.idiomatic: The crown was eight cun wide and one chi two cun long, of board with black exterior and xuan lining, without tassels; it had gold ornament and jade hairpin guide, group cords for the chin strap colored like the sash, and huang yarn ear-fillers.

sentences.zh: 大裘，繒表，黑羔表為緣，纁裏，黑領、褾、襟緣，朱裳，白紗中單，皂領，青褾、襈、裾，朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Great fur robe with silk outside, black lamb fur as border, xuan lining, black collar, cuff, and lapel border, vermilion skirt, white gauze inner robe, black collar, azure cuff, placket, and hem, vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Fur robe had silk outside, black lamb-fur border, and xuan lining; black collar, cuffs, and lapel trim; vermilion skirt; white gauze inner robe with black collar and azure cuffs, placket, and hem; vermilion socks and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍，火珠鏢首，白玉雙佩。

translations.literal: Deer-Lu jade-fitted sword, fire-pearl dart head, white jade double pendant.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a Deer-Lu sword with jade fittings, fire-pearl dart head, and white jade double pendant.

sentences.zh: 黑組大雙綬，黑質，黑、黃、赤、白、縹、綠為純，以備天地四方之色。

translations.literal: Black-group great double sash, black substance, with black, yellow, red, white, piao, and green as borders, to complete the colors of Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: A great double sash of black group, black ground, bordered in black, yellow, red, white, piao, and green to represent Heaven, Earth, and the four directions.

sentences.zh: 廣一尺，長二丈四尺，五百首。

translations.literal: One chi wide, two zhang four chi long, five hundred tassels.
translations.idiomatic: It was one chi wide, two zhang four chi long, with five hundred tassels.

sentences.zh: 紛廣二寸四分，長六尺四寸，色如綬。

translations.literal: The fen two cun four fen wide, six chi four cun long, color like the sash.
translations.idiomatic: The fen was two cun four fen wide and six chi four cun long, matching the sash color.

sentences.zh: 又有小雙綬，長二尺六寸，色如大綬，而首半之，閒施三玉環。

translations.literal: There was also a small double sash two chi six cun long, color like the great sash but half the tassels, with three jade rings set at intervals.
translations.idiomatic: A small double sash two chi six cun long matched the great sash in color but with half the tassels and three jade rings spaced along it.

sentences.zh: 革帶，以白皮為之，以屬佩、綬、印章。

translations.literal: Leather belt made of white hide, to attach pendant, sash, and seals.
translations.idiomatic: A leather belt of white hide carried pendant, sash, and seals.

sentences.zh: 鞶囊，亦曰鞶帶，博三寸半，加金鏤玉鉤䚢。

translations.literal: Pan bag, also called pan belt, three cun and a half wide, with added gold openwork jade hook clasp.
translations.idiomatic: The pan bag — also called the pan belt — was three and a half cun wide, with added gold openwork jade hook clasp.

sentences.zh: 大帶，以素為之，以朱為裏，在腰及垂皆有裨，上以朱錦，貴正色也，下以綠錦，賤閒色也，博四寸。

translations.literal: Great belt of plain silk with vermilion lining; at waist and hanging parts there were flaps, above with vermilion brocade for noble correct color, below with green brocade for lesser secondary color, four cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: The great belt was plain silk with vermilion lining; waist and hanging sections had flaps — vermilion brocade above for the noble primary color, green brocade below for the secondary — four cun wide.

sentences.zh: 紐約，貴賤皆用青組，博三寸。

translations.literal: Knot fasteners: noble and base alike used azure groups three cun wide.
translations.idiomatic: Knot fasteners for all ranks used azure cord three cun wide.

sentences.zh: 黻以繒為之，隨裳色，上廣一尺，以象天數，下廣二尺，以象地數，長三尺，朱質，畫龍、火、山三章，以象三才，其頸五寸，兩角有肩，廣二寸，以屬革帶。

translations.literal: Fu made of silk, following skirt color; above one chi wide to symbolize Heaven's number, below two chi to symbolize Earth's number, three chi long, vermilion ground, painted with dragon, fire, and mountain in three sections to symbolize the three powers; neck five cun, both corners with shoulders two cun wide, attached to the leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: The fu apron was silk, matching the skirt hue: one chi wide above for Heaven's number, two chi below for Earth's, three chi long on vermilion ground with dragon, fire, and mountain in three panels for the three powers; a five-cun neck, two-cun shoulders at both corners, joined to the leather belt.

sentences.zh: 朝服謂之鞸，冕服謂之黻。

translations.literal: Court dress called it bian; miǎn dress called it fu.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress termed it the bian; miǎn dress termed it the fu.

sentences.zh: 衮冕者，踐祚、饗廟、征還、遣將、飲至、加元服、納后、元日受朝賀、臨軒冊拜王公之服也。

translations.literal: The Gun and Miǎn Crown was dress for ascending the throne, feasting at the temple, return from campaign, dispatching generals, drink-to-arrival, capping, receiving empress, New Year congratulations, and enthroned investiture of princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Gun Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn for enthronement, temple feasts, return from campaign, dispatching generals, victory feasts, capping, receiving an empress, New Year congratulations, and enthroned investiture of princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 廣一尺二寸，長二尺四寸，金飾玉簪導，垂白珠十二旒，朱絲組帶為纓，色如綬。

translations.literal: One chi two cun wide, two chi four cun long, gold ornament and jade hairpin guide, hanging twelve white pearl tassels, vermilion silk group cords for the chin strap, color like the sash.
translations.idiomatic: The crown was one chi two cun wide and two chi four cun long, with gold ornament and jade hairpin guide, twelve white pearl tassels, and vermilion silk group cords colored like the sash.

sentences.zh: 深青衣纁裳，十二章：日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝八章在衣；

translations.literal: Deep azure upper garment and xuan skirt, twelve emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels — eight emblems on the garment;
translations.idiomatic: Deep azure coat and xuan skirt bore twelve emblems: sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels — eight on the coat;

sentences.zh: 藻、粉米、黼、黻四章在裳。

translations.literal: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu — four emblems on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu — four on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 衣畫，裳繡，以象天地之色也。

translations.literal: Garment painted, skirt embroidered, to symbolize the colors of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The coat was painted and the skirt embroidered to represent the colors of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 自山、龍以下，每章一行為等，每行十二。

translations.literal: From mountain and dragon down, each emblem one row as a grade, twelve per row.
translations.idiomatic: From mountain and dragon downward, each emblem formed one graded row of twelve.

sentences.zh: 衣、褾、領，畫以升龍，白紗中單，黻領，青褾、襈、裾，韍繡龍、山、火三章，舄加金飾。

translations.literal: Garment, cuff, and collar painted with ascending dragon; white gauze inner robe with fu collar; azure cuff, placket, and hem; knee-guard embroidered with dragon, mountain, and fire in three sections; shoes with added gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Coat, cuffs, and collar bore painted ascending dragons; white gauze inner robe with fu collar; azure cuffs, placket, and hem; knee-guard embroidered with dragon, mountain, and fire; shoes with gold fittings.

sentences.zh: 鷩冕者，有事遠主之服也。

translations.literal: The Bi and Miǎn Crown was dress for affairs with distant lords.
translations.idiomatic: The Bi Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn when dealing with distant lords.

sentences.zh: 八旒，七章：華蟲、火、宗彝三章在衣；

translations.literal: Eight tassels, seven emblems: flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels — three emblems on the garment;
translations.idiomatic: It had eight tassels and seven emblems: flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat;

sentences.zh: 藻、粉米、黼、黻四章在裳。

translations.literal: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu — four emblems on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 毳冕者，祭海嶽之服也。

translations.literal: The Cui and Miǎn Crown was dress for sacrificing to the seas and mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Cui Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn when sacrificing to the seas and mountains.

sentences.zh: 七旒，五章：宗彝、藻、粉米在衣；

translations.literal: Seven tassels, five emblems: ancestral vessels, waterweed, and grain on the garment;
translations.idiomatic: Seven tassels and five emblems: ancestral vessels, waterweed, and grain on the coat;

sentences.zh: 黼、黻在裳。

translations.literal: fu and fu on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: fu and fu on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 絺冕者，祭社稷饗先農之服也。

translations.literal: The Xi and Miǎn Crown was dress for sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain and feasting the spirit of the plough.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn for sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain and for feasting the plough spirit.

sentences.zh: 六旒，三章：絺、粉米在衣；

translations.literal: Six tassels, three emblems: xi and grain on the garment;
translations.idiomatic: Six tassels, three emblems: xi and grain on the coat;

sentences.zh: 黼、黻在裳。

translations.literal: fu and fu on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: fu and fu on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 玄冕者，蜡祭百神、朝日、夕月之服也。

translations.literal: The Xuan and Miǎn Crown was dress for the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits, morning sacrifice to the sun, and evening sacrifice to the moon.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan Robe and Miǎn Crown were worn for the wax sacrifice to the hundred spirits, the morning sun rite, and the evening moon rite.

sentences.zh: 五旒，裳刺黼一章。

translations.literal: Five tassels, skirt embroidered with one fu emblem.
translations.idiomatic: Five tassels; the skirt bore one embroidered fu emblem.

sentences.zh: 自衮冕以下，其制一也，簪導、劍、佩、綬皆同。

translations.literal: From the Gun miǎn down the system was one, with hairpin guide, sword, pendant, and sash all the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the Gun miǎn downward the system was uniform: hairpin guide, sword, pendant, and sash were alike.

sentences.zh: 通天冠者，冬至受朝賀、祭還、燕羣臣、養老之服也。

translations.literal: The Pervading Heaven Crown was dress for receiving congratulations at the winter solstice, return from sacrifice, banqueting the ministers, and nurturing the aged.
translations.idiomatic: The Pervading Heaven Crown was worn for winter-solstice congratulations, return from sacrifice, banquets for ministers, and nurturing the aged.

sentences.zh: 二十四梁，附蟬十二首，施珠翠、博山，黑介幘，組纓翠緌，玉、犀簪導，絳紗袍，朱裏紅羅裳，白紗中單，朱領、褾、襈、裾，白裙、襦，絳紗蔽膝，白羅方心曲領，白韈，黑舄。

translations.literal: Twenty-four ridges, with twelve cicada heads attached, pearl and kingfisher and Bo Mountain ornaments, black kerchief, group cords with kingfisher tassels, jade and rhinoceros hairpin guide, deep-red gauze robe, vermilion lining and red silk skirt, white gauze inner robe with vermilion collar, cuff, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white silk square heart and curved collar, white socks, black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It had twenty-four ridges and twelve attached cicada heads, with pearl, kingfisher, and Bo Mountain ornaments, black kerchief, group cords and kingfisher tassels, jade and rhinoceros hairpin guide, deep-red gauze robe, vermilion lining and red silk skirt, white gauze inner robe with vermilion collar, cuffs, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white silk square heart and curved collar, white socks, and black shoes.

sentences.zh: 白假帶，其制垂二絛帛，以變祭服之大帶。

translations.literal: White false belt, its form hanging two silk cords, to vary from the great belt of sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: A white false belt, hung with two silk cords, substituted for the sacrificial great belt.

sentences.zh: 天子未加元服，以空頂黑介幘，雙童髻，雙玉導，加寶飾。

translations.literal: Before the Son of Heaven received the capping, he wore the open-top with black kerchief, double boy's topknots, double jade guides, with added treasure ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Before receiving the capping, the Son of Heaven wore the open-top crown with black kerchief, double boy's topknots, and double jade guides with treasure ornament added.

sentences.zh: 三品以上亦加寶飾，五品以上雙玉導，金飾，六品以下無飾。

translations.literal: Third rank and above also added treasure ornament; fifth rank and above had double jade guides with gold ornament; sixth rank and below had no ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above added treasure ornament as well; fifth rank and above used double jade guides with gold ornament; sixth rank and below had none.

sentences.zh: 緇布冠者，始冠之服也。

translations.literal: The black-cloth cap was dress for the first capping.
translations.idiomatic: The black-cloth cap was worn for the first capping ceremony.

sentences.zh: 天子五梁，三品以上三梁，五品以上二梁，九品以上一梁。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had five ridges; third rank and above three ridges; fifth rank and above two ridges; ninth rank and above one ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's cap had five ridges; third rank and above three; fifth rank and above two; ninth rank and above one.

sentences.zh: 武弁者，講武、出征、蒐狩、大射、禡、類、宜社、賞祖、罰社、纂嚴之服也。

translations.literal: The martial cap was dress for martial lectures, campaign, hunt, great archery, war-prayer, battle-array, appropriate-altar and reward-ancestor, punish-altar, and mustering strictness.
translations.idiomatic: The martial cap was worn for martial lectures, campaigns, hunts, great archery, war-prayer rites, battle-array rites, offerings at the appropriate altar and reward-ancestor rites, punish-altar rites, and mustering under strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 有金附蟬，平巾幘。

translations.literal: It had gold-attached cicada and the flat kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: It bore a gold-attached cicada and the flat kerchief.

sentences.zh: 弁服者，朔日受朝之服也。

translations.literal: The bian dress was dress for receiving court on the first day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The bian dress was worn when receiving court on the first of the month.

sentences.zh: 以鹿皮為之，有攀以持髮，十有二𤪌，玉簪導，絳紗衣，素裳。

translations.literal: Made of deerskin, with loops to hold the hair, twelve tassels, jade hairpin guide, deep-red gauze upper garment, plain skirt.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of deerskin with loops to secure the hair, twelve tassels, and jade hairpin guide, with a deep-red gauze coat and plain skirt.

sentences.zh: 白玉雙佩，革帶之後有鞶囊，以盛小雙綬，白韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: White jade double pendant; behind the leather belt was a pan bag to hold the small double sash; white socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a white jade double pendant; behind the leather belt hung a pan bag for the small double sash, with white socks and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘者，拜陵之服也。

translations.literal: The black kerchief was dress for worship at tombs.
translations.idiomatic: The black kerchief was worn when worshiping at imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 無飾，白紗單衣，白裙、襦，革帶，素韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Without ornament, white gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt, plain socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It had no ornament: white gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt, plain socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 白紗冒者，視朝、聽訟、宴見賓客之服也。

translations.literal: The white gauze cap was dress for viewing court, hearing lawsuits, and banqueting and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: The white gauze cap was worn for holding court, hearing lawsuits, and banquets with guests.

sentences.zh: 以烏紗為之，白裙、襦，白韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Made of black gauze, with white skirt and jacket, white socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of black gauze, with white skirt and jacket, white socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘者，乘馬之服也。

translations.literal: The flat kerchief was dress for riding horses.
translations.idiomatic: The flat kerchief was riding dress.

sentences.zh: 金飾，玉簪導，冠支以玉，紫褶，白袴，玉具裝，珠寶鈿帶，有鞾。

translations.literal: Gold ornament, jade hairpin guide, crown branches of jade, purple pleated coat, white trousers, jade fittings, jeweled studded belt, with boots.
translations.idiomatic: It bore gold ornament and jade hairpin guide, jade crown branches, purple pleated coat, white trousers, jade sword fittings, jeweled studded belt, and boots.

sentences.zh: 白帢者，臨喪之服也。

translations.literal: The white kerchief was dress for attending mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The white kerchief was worn when attending mourning.

sentences.zh: 白紗單衣，烏皮履。

translations.literal: White gauze single robe, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It consisted of a white gauze single robe and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 皇后之服三：

translations.literal: The empress had three sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: The empress had three sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 褘衣者，受冊、助祭、朝會大事之服也。

translations.literal: The hui robe was dress for receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifice, and great court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The hui robe was worn for receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifice, and major court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 深青織成為之，畫翬，赤質，五色，十二等。

translations.literal: Woven deep azure, painted with pheasant, red ground, five colors, twelve grades.
translations.idiomatic: It was woven deep azure, painted with pheasant motifs on a red ground in five colors and twelve grades.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，朱羅縠褾、襈，蔽膝隨裳色，以緅領為緣，用翟為章，三等。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion silk gauze cuffs and placket, knee-guard following skirt color, with dark-red collar as border, using pheasant as emblem in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: It had a plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion silk gauze cuffs and placket, knee-guard matching the skirt, dark-red collar trim, and pheasant emblems in three grades.

sentences.zh: 青衣，革帶、大帶隨衣色，裨、紐約、佩、綬如天子，青韈，舄加金飾。

translations.literal: Azure coat; leather belt and great belt following garment color; flaps, knot fasteners, pendant, and sash like the Son of Heaven; azure socks; shoes with added gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The coat was azure; leather and great belts matched the garment; flaps, knot fasteners, pendant, and sash followed the Son of Heaven's model; azure socks; shoes with gold fittings.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣者，親蠶之服也。

translations.literal: The ju robe was dress for personally tending the silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The ju robe was worn when the empress personally tended the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 黃羅為之，不畫，蔽膝、大帶、革帶、舄隨衣色，餘同褘衣。

translations.literal: Made of yellow silk, unpainted; knee-guard, great belt, leather belt, and shoes following garment color; the rest like the hui robe.
translations.idiomatic: It was yellow silk without painting; knee-guard, great belt, leather belt, and shoes matched the garment; otherwise like the hui robe.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵襢衣者，燕見賓客之服也。

translations.literal: The studded hairpin and shan robe was dress for banquets and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: The studded hairpin and shan robe was worn for banquets and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 十二鈿，服用雜色而不畫，加雙佩小綬，去舄加履，首飾大小華十二樹，以象衮冕之旒，又有兩博鬢。

translations.literal: Twelve studs; dress of mixed colors without painting; added double pendant and small sash; removed shoes and added slippers; head ornament of large and small blossoms twelve trees to symbolize the gun miǎn tassels, with two broad side-locks.
translations.idiomatic: It bore twelve studs, mixed-color dress without painted emblems, double pendant and small sash, slippers instead of shoes, and a headdress of twelve large and small blossom trees echoing the gun miǎn tassels, with two broad side-locks.

sentences.zh: 皇太子之服六：

translations.literal: The heir apparent had six sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had six sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 衮冕者，從祀、謁廟、加元服、納妃之服也。

translations.literal: The gun miǎn was dress for following sacrifice, visiting the temple, capping, and receiving a consort.
translations.idiomatic: The gun robe and miǎn crown were worn when following sacrifice, visiting the temple, receiving the capping, or receiving a consort.

sentences.zh: 白珠九旒，紅絲組為纓，犀簪導，青纊充耳。

translations.literal: Nine white pearl tassels, red silk groups for the chin strap, rhinoceros hairpin guide, azure huang ear-fillers.
translations.idiomatic: The crown had nine white pearl tassels, red silk chin straps, rhinoceros hairpin guide, and azure huang ear-fillers.

sentences.zh: 黑衣纁裳，凡九章：龍、山、華蟲、火、宗彝在衣，藻、粉米、黼、黻在裳。

translations.literal: Black coat and xuan skirt, nine emblems in all: dragon, mountain, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat; waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Black coat and xuan skirt bore nine emblems: dragon, mountain, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat; waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黼領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, fu collar, azure cuff, placket, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: He wore a white gauze inner robe with fu collar and azure cuffs, placket, and hem.

sentences.zh: 革帶金鉤䚢，大帶，瑜玉雙佩。

translations.literal: Leather belt with gold hook clasp, great belt, fine jade double pendant.
translations.idiomatic: His leather belt had a gold hook clasp; he wore a great belt and fine jade double pendant.

sentences.zh: 朱組雙大綬，朱質，赤、白、縹、紺為純，長一丈八尺，廣九寸，三百二十首。

translations.literal: Vermilion-group double great sash, vermilion substance, with red, white, piao, and dark-blue as borders, one zhang eight chi long, nine cun wide, three hundred twenty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: A vermilion-group double great sash of vermilion ground bordered in red, white, piao, and dark blue measured one zhang eight chi by nine cun with three hundred twenty tassels.

sentences.zh: 黻隨裳色，有火、山二章。

translations.literal: Fu following skirt color, with fire and mountain in two sections.
translations.idiomatic: The fu apron matched the skirt, bearing fire and mountain in two panels.

sentences.zh: 白韈，赤舄，朱履，加金塗銀釦飾。

translations.literal: White socks, red shoes, vermilion slippers, with added gold-plated silver stud ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He wore white socks, red shoes, and vermilion slippers with gold-plated silver stud fittings.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍如天子。

translations.literal: Deer-Lu jade-fitted sword like the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: His Deer-Lu sword with jade fittings matched the Son of Heaven's.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠者，謁廟、還宮、元日朔日入朝、釋奠之服也。

translations.literal: The Far-Traveling Crown was dress for visiting the temple, returning to the palace, entering court on New Year and the first of the month, and the libation-of-paste rite.
translations.idiomatic: The Far-Traveling Crown was worn for temple visits, return to the palace, New Year and first-of-month court, and libation-of-paste rites.

sentences.zh: 以具服，遠遊冠三梁，加金博山，附蟬九首，施珠翠，黑介幘，髮纓翠緌，犀簪導，絳紗袍，紅裳，白紗中單，黑領、褾、襈、裾，白裙、襦，白假帶，方心曲領，絳紗蔽膝，白韈，黑舄。

translations.literal: With full dress: Far-Traveling Crown of three ridges, added gold Bo Mountain, nine attached cicada heads, pearl and kingfisher, black kerchief, hair cords with kingfisher tassels, rhinoceros hairpin guide, deep-red gauze robe, red skirt, white gauze inner robe with black collar, cuff, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, white false belt, square heart and curved collar, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white socks, black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Full dress paired the three-ridged Far-Traveling Crown with gold Bo Mountain, nine cicada heads, pearl and kingfisher ornament, black kerchief, kingfisher-tasseled hair cords, rhinoceros hairpin guide, deep-red gauze robe, red skirt, white gauze inner robe with black collar, cuffs, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, white false belt, square heart and curved collar, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white socks, and black shoes.

sentences.zh: 朔日入朝，通服絝褶。

translations.literal: On the first of the month entering court, he universally wore trousers and pleated coat.
translations.idiomatic: On first-of-month court days he wore trousers and pleated coat throughout.

sentences.zh: 公服者，五日常朝、元日冬至受朝之服也。

translations.literal: Court dress was dress for the five daily courts and receiving congratulations on New Year and the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress was worn for the five routine court days and for New Year and winter-solstice congratulations.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠，絳紗單衣，白裙、襦，革帶金鉤䚢，假帶，瑜玉隻佩，方心，紛，金縷鞶囊，純長六尺四寸，廣二寸四分，色如大綬。

translations.literal: Far-Traveling Crown, deep-red gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt with gold hook clasp, false belt, fine jade single pendant, square heart, fen, gold-thread pan bag, pure six chi four cun long and two cun four fen wide, color like the great sash.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised the Far-Traveling Crown, deep-red gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt with gold hook clasp, false belt, fine jade single pendant, square heart, fen, gold-thread pan bag six chi four cun by two cun four fen matching the great sash color.

sentences.zh: 烏紗冒者，視事及燕見賓客之服也。

translations.literal: The black gauze cap was dress for conducting business and banqueting and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: The black gauze cap was worn for routine business and for banquets with guests.

sentences.zh: 白裙、襦，烏皮履。

translations.literal: White skirt and jacket, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn with white skirt and jacket and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 弁服者，朔望視事之服也。

translations.literal: The bian dress was dress for viewing business on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: The bian dress was worn for conducting business on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 鹿皮為之，犀簪導，組纓九𤪌，絳紗衣，素裳，革帶，鞶囊，小綬，雙佩。

translations.literal: Made of deerskin, rhinoceros hairpin guide, group cords with nine tassels, deep-red gauze coat, plain skirt, leather belt, pan bag, small sash, double pendant.
translations.idiomatic: It was deerskin with rhinoceros hairpin guide, nine-tasseled group cords, deep-red gauze coat, plain skirt, leather belt, pan bag, small sash, and double pendant.

sentences.zh: 自具服以下，皆白韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: From full dress down, all had white socks and black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: From full dress downward, all sets used white socks and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘者，乘馬之服也。

translations.literal: The flat kerchief was dress for riding horses.
translations.idiomatic: The flat kerchief was riding dress.

sentences.zh: 金飾，犀簪導，紫裙，白袴，起梁珠寶鈿帶，鞾。

translations.literal: Gold ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, purple skirt, white trousers, raised-ridge jeweled studded belt, boots.
translations.idiomatic: It bore gold ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, purple skirt, white trousers, raised-ridge jeweled studded belt, and boots.

sentences.zh: 進德冠者，亦乘馬之服也。

translations.literal: The Advance-in-Virtue Crown was also dress for riding horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Advance-in-Virtue Crown was also riding dress.

sentences.zh: 九𤪌，加金飾，有袴褶，常服則有白裙、襦。

translations.literal: Nine tassels, with added gold ornament, with trousers and pleated coat; for everyday dress there were white skirt and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: It had nine tassels and gold ornament, with trousers and pleated coat; everyday wear added white skirt and jacket.

sentences.zh: 皇太子妃之服有三：

translations.literal: The heir apparent's consort had three sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's consort had three sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 褕翟者，受冊、助祭、朝會大事之服也。

translations.literal: The yu-di robe was dress for receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifice, and great court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The yu-di robe was worn for receiving investiture, assisting at sacrifice, and major court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 青織成，文為搖翟，青質，五色九等。

translations.literal: Azure woven, pattern of swaying pheasant, azure ground, five colors in nine grades.
translations.idiomatic: It was azure weave with swaying-pheasant pattern on an azure ground in five colors and nine grades.

sentences.zh: 素紗中單，黼領，朱羅縠褾、襈，蔽膝隨裳色，用緅為領緣，以翟為章二等。

translations.literal: Plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion silk gauze cuffs and placket, knee-guard following skirt color, dark-red collar border, pheasant emblem in two grades.
translations.idiomatic: It had plain gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion silk gauze cuffs and placket, knee-guard matching the skirt, dark-red collar border, and pheasant emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 青衣，革帶、大帶隨衣色，不朱裏，青韈，舄加金飾，佩、綬如皇太子。

translations.literal: Azure coat; leather belt and great belt following garment color, without vermilion lining; azure socks; shoes with gold ornament; pendant and sash like the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The coat was azure; leather and great belts matched the garment without vermilion lining; azure socks; gold-fitted shoes; pendant and sash like the heir apparent's.

sentences.zh: 鞠衣者，從蠶之服也。

translations.literal: The ju robe was dress for following the silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The ju robe was worn when following the empress to the silkworms.

sentences.zh: 以黃羅為之，制如褕翟，無雉，蔽膝、大帶隨衣色。

translations.literal: Made of yellow silk, made like the yu-di without pheasant, knee-guard and great belt following garment color.
translations.idiomatic: It was yellow silk like the yu-di but without pheasant motifs; knee-guard and great belt matched the garment.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵襢衣者，燕見賓客之服也。

translations.literal: The studded hairpin and shan robe was dress for banquets and receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: The studded hairpin and shan robe was worn for banquets and receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 九鈿，其服用雜色，制如鞠衣，加雙佩，小綬，去舄加履，首飾花九樹，有兩博鬢。

translations.literal: Nine studs; dress of mixed colors, made like the ju robe; added double pendant, small sash; removed shoes and added slippers; head ornament of nine blossom trees, with two broad side-locks.
translations.idiomatic: It bore nine studs and mixed-color dress like the ju robe, with double pendant and small sash, slippers instead of shoes, a nine-blossom headdress, and two broad side-locks.

sentences.zh: 羣臣之服二十有一：

translations.literal: The ministers had twenty-one sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: Ministers had twenty-one sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 衮冕者，一品之服也。

translations.literal: The gun miǎn was dress of first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The gun robe and miǎn crown were first-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 九旒，青𤪌為珠，貫三采玉，以組為纓，色如其綬。

translations.literal: Nine tassels, azure tassels as pearls, strung with three-colored jade, groups for the chin strap, color like the sash.
translations.idiomatic: The crown had nine tassels of azure beads strung with three-colored jade, with group chin straps colored like the sash.

sentences.zh: 青纊充耳，寶飾角簪導。

translations.literal: Azure huang ear-fillers, treasure-ornament horn hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: It had azure huang ear-fillers and treasure-ornament horn hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 青衣纁裳，九章：龍、山、華蟲、火、宗彝在衣，藻、粉米、黼、黻在裳，皆絳為繡遍衣。

translations.literal: Azure coat and xuan skirt, nine emblems: dragon, mountain, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat; waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt — all embroidered in deep red over the whole garment.
translations.idiomatic: Azure coat and xuan skirt bore nine emblems—dragon, mountain, flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat; waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt—all embroidered in deep red across the garment.

sentences.zh: 白紗中單，黼領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: White gauze inner robe, fu collar, azure cuff, placket, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: He wore white gauze inner robe with fu collar and azure cuffs, placket, and hem.

sentences.zh: 朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks and red shoes completed the set.

sentences.zh: 革帶鉤䚢，大帶，黻隨裳色。

translations.literal: Leather belt hook clasp, great belt, fu following skirt color.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt with hook clasp, great belt, and fu apron matching the skirt.

sentences.zh: 金寶玉飾劍鏢首，山玄玉佩。

translations.literal: Gold, treasure, and jade ornament sword dart head, mountain-dark jade pendant.
translations.idiomatic: The sword bore gold, treasure, and jade dart-head ornament; the pendant was mountain-dark jade.

sentences.zh: 綠綟綬，綠質，綠、紫、黃、赤為純，長一丈八尺，廣九寸，二百四十首。

translations.literal: Green silk sash, green substance, with green, purple, yellow, and red as borders, one zhang eight chi long, nine cun wide, two hundred forty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: A green silk sash of green ground bordered in green, purple, yellow, and red measured one zhang eight chi by nine cun with two hundred forty tassels.

sentences.zh: 郊祀太尉攝事亦服之。

translations.literal: At suburban sacrifice the Grand Marshal acting as substitute also wore it.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifice the Grand Marshal, when substituting, wore it as well.

sentences.zh: 鷩冕者，二品之服也。

translations.literal: The bi miǎn was dress of second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The bi robe and miǎn crown were second-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 八旒，青衣纁裳，七章：華蟲、火、宗彝在衣；

translations.literal: Eight tassels, azure coat and xuan skirt, seven emblems: flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat;
translations.idiomatic: Eight tassels; azure coat and xuan skirt with seven emblems—flowering creature, fire, and ancestral vessels on the coat;

sentences.zh: 藻、粉米、黼、黻在裳，銀裝劍，佩水蒼玉，紫綬、紫質，紫、黃、赤為純，長一丈六尺，廣八寸，一百八十首。

translations.literal: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt, silver-fitted sword, water-dark jade pendant, purple sash of purple substance with purple, yellow, and red as borders, one zhang six chi long, eight cun wide, one hundred eighty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: waterweed, grain, fu, and fu on the skirt; silver-fitted sword; water-dark jade pendant; purple sash of purple ground bordered in purple, yellow, and red, one zhang six chi by eight cun with one hundred eighty tassels.

sentences.zh: 革帶之後有金鏤鞶囊，金飾劍，水蒼玉佩，朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Behind the leather belt was a gold openwork pan bag, gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the leather belt hung a gold openwork pan bag; he wore a gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 毳冕者，三品之服也。

translations.literal: The cui miǎn was dress of third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The cui robe and miǎn crown were third-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 七旒，寶飾角簪導，五章：宗彝、藻、粉米在衣；

translations.literal: Seven tassels, treasure-ornament horn hairpin guide, five emblems: ancestral vessels, waterweed, and grain on the coat;
translations.idiomatic: Seven tassels and treasure-ornament horn hairpin guide; five emblems—ancestral vessels, waterweed, and grain on the coat;

sentences.zh: 黼、黻在裳。

translations.literal: fu and fu on the skirt.
translations.idiomatic: fu and fu on the skirt.

sentences.zh: 韍二章：山、火。

translations.literal: Knee-guard two sections: mountain and fire.
translations.idiomatic: The knee-guard bore two panels: mountain and fire.

sentences.zh: 紫綬如二品，金銀鏤鞶囊，金飾劍，水蒼玉佩，朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Purple sash like second rank, gold and silver openwork pan bag, gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Purple sash like second rank; gold and silver openwork pan bag; gold-ornament sword; water-dark jade pendant; vermilion socks; red shoes.

sentences.zh: 絺冕者，四品之服也。

translations.literal: The xi miǎn was dress of fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The xi robe and miǎn crown were fourth-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 六旒，三章：粉米在衣；

translations.literal: Six tassels, three emblems: grain on the coat;
translations.idiomatic: Six tassels; three emblems—grain on the coat;

sentences.zh: 黼、黻在裳，中單，青領。

translations.literal: fu and fu on the skirt, inner robe, azure collar.
translations.idiomatic: fu and fu on the skirt; inner robe with azure collar.

sentences.zh: 韍，山一章。

translations.literal: Knee-guard, one mountain section.
translations.idiomatic: The knee-guard bore one mountain panel.

sentences.zh: 銀鏤鞶囊。

translations.literal: Silver openwork pan bag.
translations.idiomatic: A silver openwork pan bag hung at the belt.

sentences.zh: 自三品以下皆青綬，青質，青、白、紅為純，長一丈四尺，廣七寸，一百四十首，金飾劍，水蒼玉佩，朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: From third rank down all had azure sash, azure substance, with azure, white, and red as borders, one zhang four chi long, seven cun wide, one hundred forty tassels, gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: From third rank downward all used an azure sash of azure ground bordered in azure, white, and red, one zhang four chi by seven cun with one hundred forty tassels, plus gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 玄冕者，五品之服也。

translations.literal: The xuan miǎn was dress of fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: The xuan robe and miǎn crown were fifth-rank dress.

sentences.zh: 以羅為之，五旒，衣、韍無章，裳刺黻一章。

translations.literal: Made of gauze, five tassels, coat and knee-guard without emblems, skirt embroidered with one fu section.
translations.idiomatic: Made of gauze with five tassels; coat and knee-guard bore no emblems; the skirt had one embroidered fu panel.

sentences.zh: 角簪導，青衣纁裳，其服用紬。

translations.literal: Horn hairpin guide, azure coat and xuan skirt, dress of coarse silk.
translations.idiomatic: Horn hairpin guide; azure coat and xuan skirt; the garment was coarse silk.

sentences.zh: 大帶及裨，外黑內黃，黑綬紺質，青紺為純，長一丈二尺，廣六寸，一百二十首。

translations.literal: Great belt and flaps, black outside and yellow inside; black sash with dark-blue substance, azure and dark-blue as borders, one zhang two chi long, six cun wide, one hundred twenty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Great belt and flaps were black outside and yellow inside; black sash of dark-blue ground bordered in azure and dark blue measured one zhang two chi by six cun with one hundred twenty tassels.

sentences.zh: 象笏，上圓下方，六品以竹木，上挫下方。

translations.literal: Ivory tablet, round above and square below; sixth rank and below used bamboo or wood, rounded above and squared below.
translations.idiomatic: Ivory court tablet, round above and square below; sixth rank and below used bamboo or wood, rounded above and squared below.

sentences.zh: 金飾劍，水蒼玉佩，朱韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-ornament sword, water-dark jade pendant, vermilion socks, and red shoes.

sentences.zh: 三品以下私祭皆服之。

translations.literal: Third rank and below all wore it for private sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and below wore it for private ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 平冕者，郊廟武舞郎之服也。

translations.literal: The level miǎn was dress of suburban and temple martial dance officers.
translations.idiomatic: The level miǎn was worn by suburban and temple martial dance officers.

sentences.zh: 黑衣絳裳，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Black coat and deep-red skirt, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised black coat, deep-red skirt, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 爵弁者，六品以下九品以上從祀之服也。

translations.literal: The jue bian was dress for following sacrifice from sixth rank down through ninth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The jue bian was worn by sixth rank and below through ninth rank and above when following sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以紬為之，無旒，黑纓，角簪導，青衣纁裳，白紗中單，青領、褾、襈、裾，革帶鉤䚢，大帶及裨內外皆緇，爵韠，白韈，赤履。

translations.literal: Made of coarse silk, without tassels, black chin strap, horn hairpin guide, azure coat and xuan skirt, white gauze inner robe, azure collar, cuff, placket, and hem, leather belt hook clasp, great belt and flaps all black inside and out, jue knee-guard, white socks, red slippers.
translations.idiomatic: Made of coarse silk without tassels, with black chin strap and horn hairpin guide; azure coat and xuan skirt; white gauze inner robe with azure collar, cuffs, placket, and hem; leather belt with hook clasp; all-black great belt and flaps; jue knee-guard; white socks; red slippers.

sentences.zh: 五品以上私祭皆服之。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above all wore it for private sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above wore it for private ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 武弁者，武官朝參、殿庭武舞郎、堂下鼓人、鼓吹桉工之服也。

translations.literal: The martial cap was dress for military officers attending court, courtyard martial dance officers, hall drummers, and wind-and-drum bench workers.
translations.idiomatic: The martial cap was worn by military officers at court, courtyard martial dancers, hall drummers, and wind-and-drum bench workers.

sentences.zh: 有平巾幘，武舞緋絲布大袖，白練𧛾襠，螣蛇起梁帶，豹文大口絝，烏皮鞾。

translations.literal: With flat kerchief; martial dancers in deep-red silk large sleeves, white practice cross-strap, teng-snake raised-ridge belt, leopard-pattern large trousers, black leather boots.
translations.idiomatic: It included the flat kerchief; martial dancers wore deep-red silk large sleeves, white practice cross-straps, teng-snake raised-ridge belt, leopard-pattern trousers, and black leather boots.

sentences.zh: 鼓人朱褠衣，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Drummers in vermilion padded coat, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Drummers wore vermilion padded coats, leather belts, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 鼓吹桉工加白練𧛾襠。

translations.literal: Wind-and-drum bench workers added white practice cross-strap.
translations.idiomatic: Wind-and-drum bench workers added white practice cross-straps.

sentences.zh: 弁服者，文官九品公事之服也。

translations.literal: The bian dress was dress for civil officials of ninth rank on public business.
translations.idiomatic: The bian dress was worn by civil officials of ninth rank and above on public business.

sentences.zh: 以鹿皮為之，通用烏紗，牙簪導。

translations.literal: Made of deerskin, universally using black gauze, ivory hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Made of deerskin with universal black gauze and ivory hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 纓：一品九𤪌，二品八𤪌，三品七𤪌，四品六𤪌，五品五𤪌，犀簪導，皆朱衣素裳，革帶，鞶囊，小綬，雙佩，白韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Chin strap: first rank nine tassels, second eight, third seven, fourth six, fifth five, rhinoceros hairpin guide — all with vermilion coat and plain skirt, leather belt, pan bag, small sash, double pendant, white socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Chin straps ran nine tassels for first rank, eight for second, seven for third, six for fourth, five for fifth, with rhinoceros hairpin guide; all wore vermilion coat and plain skirt, leather belt, pan bag, small sash, double pendant, white socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 六品以下去𤪌及鞶囊、綬、佩。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below omitted tassels, pan bag, sash, and pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below went without tassels, pan bag, sash, and pendant.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品綠衣，八品、九品青衣。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh rank green coat, eighth and ninth rank azure coat.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh rank wore green coats; eighth and ninth rank wore azure coats.

sentences.zh: 進賢冠者，文官朝參、三老五更之服也。

translations.literal: The Advance-the-Worthy Crown was dress for civil officials attending court and the Three Elders and Five More-Aged.
translations.idiomatic: The Advance-the-Worthy Crown was worn by civil officials at court and by the Three Elders and Five More-Aged.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，青緌。

translations.literal: Black kerchief, azure tassels.
translations.idiomatic: It was worn with black kerchief and azure tassels.

sentences.zh: 紛長六尺四寸，廣四寸，色如其綬。

translations.literal: Fen six chi four cun long, four cun wide, color like the sash.
translations.idiomatic: The fen measured six chi four cun by four cun, matching the sash color.

sentences.zh: 三品以上三梁，五品以上兩梁，九品以上及國官一梁，六品以下私祭皆服之。

translations.literal: Third rank and above three ridges, fifth rank and above two ridges, ninth rank and above and state officials one ridge; sixth rank and below all wore it for private sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above had three ridges, fifth and above two, ninth and above and state officials one; sixth rank and below wore it for private sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 侍中、中書令、左右散騎常侍有黃金璫，附蟬，貂尾。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary, Secretariat Director, and Left and Right Regular Attendants of the Scattered Cavalry had golden ear ornaments, attached cicada, and sable tail.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant-in-ordinary, Secretariat Director, and Left and Right Regular Attendants of the Scattered Cavalry wore golden ear ornaments with attached cicada and sable tail.

sentences.zh: 侍左者左珥，侍右者右珥。

translations.literal: Those attending on the left had left ear ornament, those on the right right ear ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants on the left wore the left ear ornament; those on the right, the right.

sentences.zh: 諸州大中正一梁，絳紗公服。

translations.literal: Grand Rectifiers of the provinces one ridge, deep-red gauze court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Grand Rectifiers wore one ridge with deep-red gauze court dress.

sentences.zh: 殿庭文舞郎，黃紗袍，黑領、襈，白練𧛾襠，白布大口絝，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Courtyard civil dance officers: yellow gauze robe, black collar and placket, white practice cross-strap, white cloth large trousers, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Courtyard civil dancers wore yellow gauze robes with black collar and placket, white practice cross-straps, white cloth trousers, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 遠遊冠者，親王之服也。

translations.literal: The Far-Traveling Crown was dress of imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: The Far-Traveling Crown was princely dress.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，三梁，青緌，金鉤䚢大帶，金寶飾劍，玉鏢首，纁朱綬，朱質，赤、黃、縹、紺為純，長一丈八尺，廣九寸，二百四十首。

translations.literal: Black kerchief, three ridges, azure tassels, great belt with gold hook clasp, gold and treasure ornament sword, jade dart head, xuan-vermilion sash of vermilion substance with red, yellow, piao, and dark-blue borders, one zhang eight chi long, nine cun wide, two hundred forty tassels.
translations.idiomatic: It paired black kerchief and three ridges with azure tassels, gold-clasp great belt, treasure-ornament sword with jade dart head, and a xuan-vermilion sash of vermilion ground bordered in red, yellow, piao, and dark blue—one zhang eight chi by nine cun with two hundred forty tassels.

sentences.zh: 黃金璫，附蟬，諸王則否。

translations.literal: Golden ear ornament and attached cicada; other princes did not.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes of certain rank wore golden ear ornaments with attached cicada; other princes did not.

sentences.zh: 法冠者，御史大夫、中丞、御史之服也。

translations.literal: The Law Crown was dress of the Censor-in-chief, Vice Censor-in-chief, and censors.
translations.idiomatic: The Law Crown was worn by the Censor-in-chief, Vice Censor-in-chief, and investigating censors.

sentences.zh: 一名解廌冠。

translations.literal: Also called the Xiezhi Crown.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the Xiezhi Crown.

sentences.zh: 高山冠者，內侍省內謁者、親王司閤、謁者之服也。

translations.literal: The Lofty Mountain Crown was dress of Inner Palace attendants, princes' gatekeepers, and ushers.
translations.idiomatic: The Lofty Mountain Crown was worn by Inner Palace attendants, princes' gatekeepers, and ushers.

sentences.zh: 委貌冠者，郊廟文舞郎之服也。

translations.literal: The Wei Mao Crown was dress of suburban and temple civil dance officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Mao Crown was worn by suburban and temple civil dancers.

sentences.zh: 有黑絲布大袖，白練領、褾，絳布大口絝，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: With black silk large sleeves, white practice collar and cuffs, deep-red cloth large trousers, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black silk large sleeves, white practice collar and cuffs, deep-red cloth trousers, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 却非冠者，亭長、門僕之服也。

translations.literal: The Quefei Crown was dress of pavilion chiefs and gate servants.
translations.idiomatic: The Quefei Crown was worn by pavilion chiefs and gate servants.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘者，武官、衞官公事之服也。

translations.literal: The flat kerchief was dress for military and guard officials on public business.
translations.idiomatic: The flat kerchief was public dress for military and guard officials.

sentences.zh: 金飾，五品以上兼用玉，大口絝，烏皮鞾，白練裙、襦，起梁帶。

translations.literal: Gold ornament; fifth rank and above also used jade; large trousers, black leather boots, white practice skirt and jacket, raised-ridge belt.
translations.idiomatic: It bore gold ornament—fifth rank and above also jade—large trousers, black leather boots, white practice skirt and jacket, and raised-ridge belt.

sentences.zh: 陪大仗，有裲襠、螣蛇。

translations.literal: When accompanying the great guard, they had armor vest and teng-snake.
translations.idiomatic: When escorting the great guard they added an armor vest and teng-snake streamer.

sentences.zh: 朝集從事、州縣佐史、岳瀆祝史、外州品子、庶民任掌事者服之，有緋褶、大口絝，紫附褠。

translations.literal: Assembly clerks, prefectural and county clerks, mountain-and-river prayer officers, outside-province candidates, and commoners charged with duties wore it, with deep-red pleated coat, large trousers, and purple attached padded coat.
translations.idiomatic: Assembly clerks, prefectural and county clerks, mountain-and-river prayer officers, outside-province candidates, and commoners on official duty wore it with deep-red pleated coat, large trousers, and purple attached padded coat.

sentences.zh: 文武官騎馬服之，則去裲襠、螣蛇。

translations.literal: When civil and military officials wore it for riding horses, they removed armor vest and teng-snake.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials wore it for riding without the armor vest and teng-snake.

sentences.zh: 袴褶之制：五品以上，細綾及羅為之，六品以下，小綾為之，三品以上紫，五品以上緋，七品以上綠，九品以上碧。

translations.literal: Regulations for trousers and pleated coat: fifth rank and above used fine damask and gauze; sixth rank and below small damask; third rank and above purple, fifth rank and above deep red, seventh rank and above green, ninth rank and above blue-green.
translations.idiomatic: Trousers and pleated coats for fifth rank and above were fine damask or gauze; sixth and below used small damask; colors ran purple for third rank and above, deep red for fifth, green for seventh, blue-green for ninth.

sentences.zh: 裲襠之制：一當胸，一當背，短袖覆膊。

translations.literal: Regulations for armor vest: one for chest, one for back, short sleeves covering the upper arm.
translations.idiomatic: The armor vest had one panel for the chest and one for the back, with short sleeves covering the upper arms.

sentences.zh: 螣蛇之制：以錦為表，長八尺，中實以綿，象蛇形。

translations.literal: Regulations for teng-snake: brocade outside, eight chi long, stuffed with cotton within, shaped like a snake.
translations.idiomatic: The teng-snake streamer used brocade outside, eight chi long, cotton-stuffed within, and shaped like a serpent.

sentences.zh: 起梁帶之制：三品以上，玉梁寶鈿，五品以上，金梁寶鈿，六品以下，金飾隱起而已。

translations.literal: Regulations for raised-ridge belt: third rank and above jade ridge with treasure studs; fifth rank and above gold ridge with treasure studs; sixth rank and below gold ornament in low relief only.
translations.idiomatic: Raised-ridge belts for third rank and above had jade ridge and treasure studs; fifth and above gold ridge and treasure studs; sixth and below only low-relief gold ornament.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘者，國官視品、府佐謁府、國子大學四門生俊士參見之服也。

translations.literal: The black kerchief was dress for state officials by nominal rank, prefectural assistants visiting the prefecture, and Guozi University Four Gates outstanding students presenting themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The black kerchief was worn by state officials of nominal rank, prefectural assistants on prefectural visits, and outstanding Guozi Four Gates students presenting themselves.

sentences.zh: 簪導，白紗單衣，青襟、褾、領，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Hairpin guide, white gauze single robe, azure lapel, cuff, and collar, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It included hairpin guide, white gauze single robe with azure lapel, cuffs, and collar, leather belt, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 未冠者，冠則空頂黑介幘，雙童髻，去革帶。

translations.literal: Those not yet capped, when capped used open-top black kerchief, double boy's topknots, removing leather belt.
translations.idiomatic: The uncapped wore open-top black kerchief and double boy's topknots when capped, without leather belt.

sentences.zh: 書算律學生、州縣學生朝參，則服烏紗冒，白裙、襦，青領。

translations.literal: Writing, calculation, and law students and prefectural and county students attending court wore black gauze cap, white skirt and jacket, azure collar.
translations.idiomatic: Writing, calculation, and law students and prefectural students at court wore black gauze cap, white skirt and jacket, and azure collar.

sentences.zh: 未冠者童子髻。

translations.literal: Those not yet capped used boy's topknot.
translations.idiomatic: Uncapped students wore the boy's topknot.

sentences.zh: 介幘者，流外官、行署三品以下、登歌工人之服也。

translations.literal: The kerchief was dress for outside-the-register officials, traveling-office third rank and below, and hymn singers.
translations.idiomatic: The kerchief was worn by outside-the-register officials, traveling-office staff of third rank and below, and hymn singers.

sentences.zh: 絳公服，以縵緋為之，制如絳紗單衣，方心曲領，革帶鉤䚢，假帶，韈，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Deep-red court dress made of plain deep-red silk, made like deep-red gauze single robe, square heart and curved collar, leather belt hook clasp, false belt, socks, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Deep-red court dress of plain deep-red silk followed the deep-red gauze single robe with square heart and curved collar, leather belt hook clasp, false belt, socks, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 九品以上則絳褠衣，制如絳公服而狹，袖形直如溝，不垂，緋褶大口絝，紫附褠，去方心曲領、假帶。

translations.literal: Ninth rank and above had deep-red padded coat, made like deep-red court dress but narrow, sleeves straight like a ditch without hanging, deep-red pleated large trousers, purple attached padding, removing square heart, curved collar, and false belt.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank and above wore a deep-red padded coat like court dress but narrower, with straight non-hanging sleeves, deep-red pleated trousers, purple attached padding, and no square heart, curved collar, or false belt.

sentences.zh: 登歌工人，朱連裳，革帶，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Hymn singers: vermilion linked robe, leather belt, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Hymn singers wore vermilion linked robes, leather belts, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 殿庭加白練𧛾襠。

translations.literal: In the courtyard they added white practice cross-strap.
translations.idiomatic: In the courtyard they added white practice cross-straps.

sentences.zh: 平巾綠幘者，尚食局主膳，典膳局典食，太官署、食官署供膳、奉觶之服也。

translations.literal: The flat kerchief with green band was dress of the Bureau of Imperial Viands chief cooks, Bureau of Palace Viands food officers, Grand Steward and Food Service bureaus food preparers and cup bearers.
translations.idiomatic: The green-banded flat kerchief was worn by chief cooks of the Bureau of Imperial Viands, food officers of the Bureau of Palace Viands, and food preparers and cup bearers of the Grand Steward and Food Service bureaus.

sentences.zh: 青絲布絝褶。

translations.literal: Azure silk trousers and pleated coat.
translations.idiomatic: They wore azure silk trousers and pleated coat.

sentences.zh: 羊車小史，五辮髻，紫碧腰襻，青耳屩。

translations.literal: Goat-chariot clerks: five-plait topknot, purple and blue waist sash, azure ear slippers.
translations.idiomatic: Goat-chariot clerks wore five-plait topknots, purple-and-blue waist sashes, and azure ear slippers.

sentences.zh: 漏刻生、漏童，總角髻，皆青絲布絝褶。

translations.literal: Clepsydra students and clepsydra boys, total-angle topknots, all in azure silk trousers and pleated coat.
translations.idiomatic: Clepsydra students and boys wore total-angle topknots and azure silk trousers and pleated coats.

sentences.zh: 具服者，五品以上陪祭、朝饗、拜表、大事之服也，亦曰朝服。

translations.literal: Full dress was dress for fifth rank and above accompanying sacrifice, morning banquets, presenting memorials, and great affairs — also called court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Full dress was worn by fifth rank and above for accompanying sacrifice, morning banquets, memorial presentation, and major affairs—also called court dress.

sentences.zh: 冠幘，簪導，絳紗單衣，白紗中單，黑領、袖，黑褾、襈、裾，白裙、襦，革帶金鉤䚢，假帶，曲領方心，絳紗蔽膝，白韈，烏皮舄，劍，紛，鞶囊，雙佩，雙綬。

translations.literal: Crown and kerchief, hairpin guide, deep-red gauze single robe, white gauze inner robe, black collar and sleeves, black cuff, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, leather belt with gold hook clasp, false belt, curved collar and square heart, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white socks, black leather shoes, sword, fen, pan bag, double pendant, double sash.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised crown and kerchief, hairpin guide, deep-red gauze single robe, white gauze inner robe with black collar, sleeves, cuffs, placket, and hem, white skirt and jacket, gold-clasp leather belt, false belt, curved collar and square heart, deep-red gauze knee-guard, white socks, black leather shoes, sword, fen, pan bag, double pendant, and double sash.

sentences.zh: 六品以下去劍、佩、綬，七品以上以白筆代簪，八品、九品去白筆，白紗中單，以履代舄。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below removed sword, pendant, and sash; seventh rank and above used white brush in place of hairpin; eighth and ninth rank removed white brush; white gauze inner robe; used slippers in place of shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below went without sword, pendant, and sash; seventh and above substituted a white brush for the hairpin; eighth and ninth dropped the brush; all used white gauze inner robe and slippers instead of shoes.

sentences.zh: 從省服者，五品以上公事、朔望朝謁、見東宮之服也，亦曰公服。

translations.literal: Reduced dress was dress for fifth rank and above on public business, first-and-fifteenth court attendance, and audience with the heir apparent — also called court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Reduced dress was worn by fifth rank and above for public business, first-and-fifteenth court days, and audiences with the heir apparent—also called court dress.

sentences.zh: 冠幘纓，簪導，絳紗單衣，白裙、襦，革帶鉤䚢，假帶，方心，韈，履，紛，鞶囊，雙佩，烏皮履。

translations.literal: Crown, kerchief, and chin strap, hairpin guide, deep-red gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt hook clasp, false belt, square heart, socks, slippers, fen, pan bag, double pendant, black leather shoes.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised crown, kerchief, and chin strap, hairpin guide, deep-red gauze single robe, white skirt and jacket, leather belt with hook clasp, false belt, square heart, socks, slippers, fen, pan bag, double pendant, and black leather shoes.

sentences.zh: 六品以下去紛、鞶囊、雙佩。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and below removed fen, pan bag, and double pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and below went without fen, pan bag, and double pendant.

sentences.zh: 三品以上有公爵者，嫡子之婚，假絺冕。

translations.literal: Third rank and above with ducal title: at the principal son's wedding, borrowed xi miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above holding a ducal title lent the xi miǎn for a principal son's wedding.

sentences.zh: 五品以上子孫，九品以上子，爵弁。

translations.literal: Descendants of fifth rank and above, sons of ninth rank and above, jue bian.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of fifth rank and above and sons of ninth rank and above wore the jue bian.

sentences.zh: 庶人婚，假絳公服。

translations.literal: Commoners at wedding borrowed deep-red court dress.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners at weddings borrowed deep-red court dress.

sentences.zh: 命婦之服六：

translations.literal: Wives by imperial grant had six sets of dress:
translations.idiomatic: Wives holding titles by imperial grant had six sets of dress:

sentences.zh: 翟衣者，內命婦受冊、從蠶、朝會，外命婦嫁及受冊、從蠶、大朝會之服也。
