translations.literal: The di robe was dress for inner-title wives receiving investiture, following the silkworms, and court assemblies; for outer-title wives at marriage and receiving investiture, following silkworms, and great court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: The di robe was worn by inner-title wives for investiture, following the silkworms, and court; by outer-title wives for marriage, investiture, following silkworms, and great assemblies.

sentences.zh: 青質，繡翟，編次於衣及裳，重為九等。

translations.literal: Azure substance, embroidered pheasant, arrayed in grades on coat and skirt, nine grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: It was azure ground with embroidered pheasant arrayed in nine graded rows on coat and skirt.

sentences.zh: 青紗中單，黼領，朱縠褾、襈、裾，蔽膝隨裳色，以緅為領緣，加文繡，重雉為章二等。

translations.literal: Azure gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion gauze cuffs, placket, and hem, knee-guard following skirt color, dark-red collar border, added patterned embroidery, double pheasant emblems in two grades.
translations.idiomatic: It had azure gauze inner robe, fu collar, vermilion gauze cuffs, placket, and hem, knee-guard matching the skirt, dark-red collar border, added patterned embroidery, and double pheasant emblems in two grades.

sentences.zh: 大帶隨衣色，以青衣，革帶，青韈，舄，佩，綬，兩博鬢飾以寶鈿。

translations.literal: Great belt following garment color, with azure coat, leather belt, azure socks, shoes, pendant, sash, two broad side-locks ornamented with treasure studs.
translations.idiomatic: Great belt matched the garment; azure coat; leather belt; azure socks and shoes; pendant and sash; two broad side-locks with treasure studs.

sentences.zh: 一品翟九等，花釵九樹；

translations.literal: First rank di nine grades, blossom hairpin nine trees;
translations.idiomatic: First rank: di in nine grades, blossom hairpin of nine trees;

sentences.zh: 二品翟八等，花釵八樹；

translations.literal: Second rank di eight grades, blossom hairpin eight trees;
translations.idiomatic: second rank: eight grades and eight trees;

sentences.zh: 三品翟七等，花釵七樹；

translations.literal: Third rank di seven grades, blossom hairpin seven trees;
translations.idiomatic: third rank: seven and seven;

sentences.zh: 四品翟六等，花釵六樹；

translations.literal: Fourth rank di six grades, blossom hairpin six trees;
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank: six and six;

sentences.zh: 五品翟五等，花釵五樹。

translations.literal: Fifth rank di five grades, blossom hairpin five trees.
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank: five and five.

sentences.zh: 寶鈿視花樹之數。

translations.literal: Treasure studs followed the number of blossom trees.
translations.idiomatic: Treasure studs matched the number of blossom trees.

sentences.zh: 鈿釵禮衣者，內命婦常參、外命婦朝參、辭見、禮會之服也。

translations.literal: The studded hairpin ceremonial robe was dress for inner-title wives at routine attendance, outer-title wives at court attendance, farewell audiences, and ceremonial gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: The studded hairpin ceremonial robe was worn by inner-title wives at routine attendance and by outer-title wives for court, farewell audiences, and ceremonial gatherings.

sentences.zh: 制同翟衣，加雙佩、小綬，去舄，加履。

translations.literal: Made like the di robe, added double pendant and small sash, removed shoes and added slippers.
translations.idiomatic: Like the di robe, it added double pendant and small sash and substituted slippers for shoes.

sentences.zh: 一品九鈿，二品八鈿，三品七鈿，四品六鈿，五品五鈿。

translations.literal: First rank nine studs, second eight, third seven, fourth six, fifth five.
translations.idiomatic: Studs ran nine for first rank, eight for second, seven for third, six for fourth, five for fifth.

sentences.zh: 禮衣者，六尚、寶林、御女、采女、女官七品以上大事之服也。

translations.literal: Ceremonial robe was dress for the Six Bureaus, Treasure Forest, palace women, selected women, and female officials of seventh rank and above on great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial robe was worn by the Six Bureaus, Treasure Forest, palace women, selected women, and female officials of seventh rank and above on major occasions.

sentences.zh: 通用雜色，制如鈿釵禮衣，唯無首飾、佩、綬。

translations.literal: Universally mixed colors, made like the studded hairpin ceremonial robe, only without head ornament, pendant, or sash.
translations.idiomatic: It used mixed colors like the studded hairpin ceremonial robe but without head ornament, pendant, or sash.

sentences.zh: 公服者，常供奉之服也。

translations.literal: Court dress was dress for routine attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress was routine attendance dress.

sentences.zh: 去中單、蔽膝、大帶，九品以上大事、常供奉亦如之。

translations.literal: Removed inner robe, knee-guard, and great belt; ninth rank and above on great affairs and routine attendance likewise.
translations.idiomatic: It omitted inner robe, knee-guard, and great belt; ninth rank and above did the same for major affairs and routine attendance.

sentences.zh: 半袖裙襦者，東宮女史常供奉之服也。

translations.literal: Half-sleeve skirt and jacket was dress for Eastern Palace female clerks on routine attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Half-sleeve skirt and jacket was worn by Eastern Palace female clerks on routine attendance.

sentences.zh: 公主、王妃佩、綬同諸王。

translations.literal: Princesses and imperial sons' consorts: pendant and sash like princes.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and imperial sons' consorts used pendant and sash like princes.

sentences.zh: 花釵禮衣者，親王納妃所給之服也。

translations.literal: Blossom hairpin ceremonial robe was dress given when an imperial prince received a consort.
translations.idiomatic: The blossom hairpin ceremonial robe was granted when an imperial prince received a consort.

sentences.zh: 大袖連裳者，六品以下妻，九品以上女嫁服也。

translations.literal: Large-sleeve linked robe was marriage dress for wives of sixth rank and below and daughters of ninth rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: The large-sleeve linked robe was marriage dress for wives below sixth rank and daughters of ninth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 青質，素紗中單，蔽膝、大帶、革帶，韈、履同裳色，花釵，覆笄，兩博鬢，以金銀雜寶飾之。

translations.literal: Azure substance, plain gauze inner robe, knee-guard and great belt and leather belt, socks and slippers like skirt color, blossom hairpin, covered hairpin, two broad side-locks, ornamented with mixed gold, silver, and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: Azure ground, plain gauze inner robe, knee-guard, great belt, and leather belt, socks and slippers matching the skirt, blossom hairpin, covered hairpin, two broad side-locks ornamented in gold, silver, and jewels.

sentences.zh: 庶人女嫁有花釵，以金銀琉璃塗飾之。

translations.literal: Commoner daughters at marriage had blossom hairpin, ornamented with gold, silver, and glazed coating.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner brides wore blossom hairpins ornamented in gold, silver, and glazed coating.

sentences.zh: 連裳，青質，青衣，革帶，韈、履同裳色。

translations.literal: Linked robe, azure substance, azure coat, leather belt, socks and slippers like skirt color.
translations.idiomatic: The linked robe was azure throughout—coat, leather belt, socks, and slippers matching the skirt.

sentences.zh: 婦人燕服視夫。

translations.literal: Women's informal dress followed the husband.
translations.idiomatic: Women's informal dress followed their husbands' rank.

sentences.zh: 百官女嫁、廟見攝母服。

translations.literal: Officials' daughters at marriage and temple audience acting as mother wore accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' daughters at marriage and acting as mother at temple audience dressed by the corresponding rules.

sentences.zh: 五品以上媵降妻一等，妾降媵一等，六品以下妾降妻一等。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above: secondary wives one grade below wife, concubines one grade below secondary wife; sixth rank and below concubines one grade below wife.
translations.idiomatic: From fifth rank up, secondary wives ranked one grade below the wife and concubines one below secondary wives; from sixth rank down, concubines ranked one grade below the wife.

sentences.zh: 天子有傳國璽及八璽，皆玉為之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had the transmission-of-the-realm seal and eight seals, all made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven possessed the transmission-of-the-realm seal and eight jade seals.

sentences.zh: 神璽以鎮中國，藏而不用。

translations.literal: The Spirit Seal to stabilize the Central Kingdom was stored and not used.
translations.idiomatic: The Spirit Seal that stabilized the Central Kingdom was kept in store and never used.

sentences.zh: 受命璽以封禪禮神，皇帝行璽以報王公書，皇帝之璽以勞王公，皇帝信璽以召王公，天子行璽以報四夷書，天子之璽以勞四夷，天子信璽以召兵四夷，皆泥封。

translations.literal: The Mandate-Receiving Seal for feng and shan and sacrificing to the spirits; the Emperor's Progress Seal for replying to princes and dukes in writing; the Emperor's Seal for rewarding princes and dukes; the Emperor's Trust Seal for summoning princes and dukes; the Son of Heaven's Progress Seal for replying to the four barbarians in writing; the Son of Heaven's Seal for rewarding the four barbarians; the Son of Heaven's Trust Seal for summoning troops of the four barbarians — all with mud seals.
translations.idiomatic: The Mandate-Receiving Seal served feng, shan, and spirit sacrifice; the Emperor's Progress Seal answered letters to princes and dukes; the Emperor's Seal rewarded them; the Emperor's Trust Seal summoned them; the Son of Heaven's Progress Seal answered the four quarters; the Son of Heaven's Seal rewarded them; the Son of Heaven's Trust Seal summoned their troops—all sealed with mud.

sentences.zh: 大朝會則符璽郎進神璽、受命璽於御座，行幸則合八璽為五輿，函封從於黃鉞之內。

translations.literal: At great court assemblies the Seal Officer advanced the Spirit Seal and Mandate-Receiving Seal to the imperial seat; on progress the eight seals were combined into five carriages, cased and sealed and followed within the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: At great assemblies the Seal Officer presented the Spirit and Mandate-Receiving seals to the throne; on progress the eight seals were packed into five cases, sealed, and borne within the yellow battle-axe escort.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后、皇后、皇太子及妃，璽皆金為之，藏而不用。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Empress, heir apparent and consort — their seals were all gold, stored and not used.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Empress, heir apparent, and consort all had gold seals kept in store unused.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后封令書以宮官印，皇后以內侍省印，皇太子以左春坊印，妃以內坊印。

translations.literal: Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager sealed command documents with palace-official seals; Empress with Inner Service seal; heir apparent with Left Spring Palace seal; consort with Inner Quarters seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager used palace-official seals on commands; the Empress the Inner Service seal; the heir apparent the Left Spring Palace seal; the consort the Inner Quarters seal.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗刻受命玄璽，以白玉為螭首，文曰：「皇天景命，有德者昌。

translations.literal: At first Taizong carved the Mandate-Receiving Dark Seal, with white jade dragon head, inscription reading: "August Heaven's bright mandate — the virtuous shall flourish.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taizong carved the Mandate-Receiving Dark Seal with a white jade dragon head inscribed: "August Heaven's bright mandate — the virtuous shall flourish.

sentences.zh: 」至武后改諸璽皆為寶。

translations.literal: " When Empress Wu later changed all seals to treasures.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Wu later changed all seals to treasures.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，復為璽。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, they were restored to seals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong restored them to seals on his accession.

sentences.zh: 開元六年，復為寶。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaiyuan, they were again made treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan year 6 they were again termed treasures.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，改璽書為寶書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, seal documents were changed to treasure documents.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao, seal documents became treasure documents.

sentences.zh: 十載，改傳國寶為承天大寶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the transmission-of-the-realm treasure was changed to the Receive-Heaven Great Treasure.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 the transmission treasure was renamed the Receive-Heaven Great Treasure.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖入長安，罷隋竹使符，班銀菟符，其後改為銅魚符，以起軍旅、易守長，京都留守、折衝府、捉兵鎮守之所及左右金吾、宮苑總監、牧監皆給之。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu entered Chang'an, Sui bamboo tally tokens were abolished and silver hare tokens issued; afterward they were changed to bronze fish tokens to raise armies and replace prefects and magistrates — the capital garrison, defense commands, troop-mustering garrisons, Left and Right Gold Crow guards, palace parks, chief stewards, and pasture supervisors all received them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first entered Chang'an he abolished Sui bamboo tallies and issued silver hare tokens; later these became bronze fish tallies to mobilize troops and replace prefects and magistrates—issued to the capital garrison, defense commands, garrisons, Left and Right Gold Crow guards, palace parks, chief stewards, and pasture supervisors.

sentences.zh: 畿內則左三右一，畿外則左五右一，左者進內，右者在外，用始第一，周而復始。

translations.literal: Within the capital precincts, three on the left and one on the right; outside the precincts, five on the left and one on the right; the left advanced inward, the right remained outside, starting from number one and cycling.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the capital there were three left tallies and one right; outside, five left and one right—the left set went inward, the right stayed out, numbered from one and cycling.

sentences.zh: 宮殿門、城門，給交魚符、巡魚符。

translations.literal: Palace gates and city gates were given intersecting fish tokens and patrol fish tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and city gates received intersecting fish and patrol fish tokens.

sentences.zh: 左廂、右廂給開門符、閉門符。

translations.literal: Left and right wings were given open-gate and close-gate tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right wings received open-gate and close-gate tokens.

sentences.zh: 亦左符進內，右符監門掌之。

translations.literal: Likewise the left token advanced inward and the right token was kept by the gate wardens.
translations.idiomatic: Again the left tally went inward and the right was held by gate wardens.

sentences.zh: 蕃國亦給之，雄雌各十二，銘以國名，雄者進內，雌者付其國。

translations.literal: Foreign states also received them, twelve male and twelve female, inscribed with the state name; the male advanced inward, the female was given to that state.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign states received them too—twelve male and twelve female, inscribed with the state name; males went inward, females to the state.

sentences.zh: 朝貢使各齎其月魚而至，不合者劾奏。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys each carried their month's fish on arrival; mismatches were impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute envoys each brought that month's fish tally; mismatches were impeached.

sentences.zh: 傳信符者，以給郵驛，通制命。

translations.literal: Transmission tokens were given to postal stations to convey imperial orders.
translations.idiomatic: Transmission tokens were issued to postal stations to convey imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 皇太子監國給雙龍符，左右皆十。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent supervised the state, double-dragon tokens were given, ten on each side.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent supervised the realm he received double-dragon tokens, ten left and ten right.

sentences.zh: 兩京、北都留守給麟符，左二十，右十九。

translations.literal: The two capitals and Northern Capital garrisons received qilin tokens, twenty on the left and nineteen on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons of the two capitals and Northern Capital received qilin tokens—twenty left, nineteen right.

sentences.zh: 東方諸州給青龍符，南方諸州朱雀符，西方諸州騶虞符，北方諸州玄武符，皆左四右三。

translations.literal: Eastern provinces received azure-dragon tokens, southern provinces vermilion-bird tokens, western provinces zouyu tokens, northern provinces black-tortoise tokens — all four on the left and three on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern provinces received azure-dragon tokens, southern vermilion-bird, western zouyu, northern black-tortoise—four left and three right each.

sentences.zh: 左者進內，右者付外。

translations.literal: The left advanced inward, the right was given outside.
translations.idiomatic: Left tallies went inward; right tallies were issued outward.

sentences.zh: 行軍所亦給之。

translations.literal: Campaign headquarters also received them.
translations.idiomatic: Field headquarters received them as well.

sentences.zh: 隨身魚符者，以明貴賤，應召命，左二右一，左者進內，右者隨身。

translations.literal: Personal fish tokens marked noble and base and answered summons; two on the left and one on the right — the left advanced inward, the right was carried on the person.
translations.idiomatic: Personal fish tokens marked rank and answered summons: two left, one right—the left went inward, the right was worn on the person.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以玉契召，勘合乃赴。

translations.literal: The heir apparent summoned with jade tally; only after verification did one attend.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent summoned with a jade tally; attendance followed only after verification.

sentences.zh: 親王以金，庶官以銅，皆題某位姓名。

translations.literal: Imperial princes used gold, common officials copper, all inscribed with office and personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes used gold tallies, common officials copper, each inscribed with office and name.

sentences.zh: 官有貳者加左右，皆盛以魚袋，三品以上飾以金，五品以上飾以銀。

translations.literal: Offices with deputies added left and right; all were kept in fish bags — third rank and above ornamented with gold, fifth rank and above with silver.
translations.idiomatic: Duplicate posts added left and right tallies, all kept in fish bags—gold for third rank and above, silver for fifth and above.

sentences.zh: 刻姓名者，去官納之，不刻者傳佩相付。

translations.literal: Those with engraved names surrendered them on leaving office; those without engraving passed them on in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Engraved tallies were surrendered on leaving office; unengraved ones passed from holder to holder.

sentences.zh: 有傳符、銅魚符者，給封符印，發驛、封符及封魚函用之。

translations.literal: Those with transmission tokens and bronze fish tokens were given seal tokens for dispatching couriers, sealing dispatches, and sealing fish cases.
translations.idiomatic: Holders of transmission and bronze fish tokens received seal tokens for couriers, sealed dispatches, and sealed fish cases.

sentences.zh: 有銅魚而無傳符者，給封函，還符、封函用之。

translations.literal: Those with bronze fish but without transmission tokens were given seal cases, used when returning tokens and sealing cases.
translations.idiomatic: Those with bronze fish but no transmission token received seal cases for returning tokens and sealing correspondence.

sentences.zh: 天子巡幸，則京師、東都留守給留守印，諸司從行者，給行從印。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven toured, the capital and Eastern Capital garrisons were given garrison seals; offices accompanying him were given progress seals.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial tours the capital and Luoyang garrisons received garrison seals; accompanying offices received progress seals.

sentences.zh: 木契符者，以重鎮守、慎出納，畿內左右皆三，畿外左右皆五。

translations.literal: Wooden tally tokens were for weighty garrison defense and careful receipt and disbursement — three left and three right within the capital precincts, five left and five right outside.
translations.idiomatic: Wooden tally tokens secured major garrisons and controlled receipts and disbursements—three left and three right inside the capital, five each side outside.

sentences.zh: 皇帝巡幸，太子監國，有軍旅之事則用之，王公征討皆給焉，左右各十九。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured, the heir apparent supervised the state, or when military affairs arose, they were used; princes and dukes on campaign all received them, nineteen on each side.
translations.idiomatic: They were used when the emperor toured, the heir apparent supervised the realm, or military affairs arose; campaigning princes and dukes each received nineteen left and right.

sentences.zh: 太極殿前刻漏所，亦以左契給之，右以授承天門監門，晝夜勘合，然後鳴鼓。

translations.literal: The clepsydra office before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate also received the left tally on the left; the right was given to the Chengtian Gate wardens — only after day-and-night verification was the drum sounded.
translations.idiomatic: The clepsydra office before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate held the left tally; the right went to Chengtian Gate wardens—drums sounded only after day-and-night verification.

sentences.zh: 玄武門苑內諸門有喚人木契，左以進內，右以授監門，有敕召者用之。

translations.literal: The Xuanwu Gate park inner gates had summoning wooden tallies; the left advanced inward, the right was given to gate wardens for use when there was an edict summons.
translations.idiomatic: Inner gates of the Xuanwu park had summoning wooden tallies—left inward, right to gate wardens—for edict summons.

sentences.zh: 魚契所降，皆有敕書。

translations.literal: Fish tallies issued downward all had accompanying edict documents.
translations.idiomatic: Every fish tally issued downward came with an edict.

sentences.zh: 尚書省符，與左同乃用。

translations.literal: Ministry of State Affairs tokens were used only when matching the left.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry tokens were valid only when matched to the left tally.

sentences.zh: 大將出，賜旌以顓賞，節以顓殺。

translations.literal: When great generals went out, banners were bestowed for conspicuous reward and staffs for conspicuous execution.
translations.idiomatic: Departing great generals received banners for conspicuous reward and staffs for conspicuous execution.

sentences.zh: 旌以絳帛五丈，粉畫虎，有銅龍一，首纏緋幡，紫縑為袋，油囊為表。

translations.literal: The banner was five zhang of deep-red silk, powder-painted with a tiger, one bronze dragon, head wrapped in deep-red pennant, purple silk as bag, oil skin as cover.
translations.idiomatic: The banner was five zhang of deep-red silk powder-painted with a tiger, bearing one bronze dragon, deep-red pennant at the head, purple silk bag, and oilskin cover.

sentences.zh: 節，懸畫木盤三，相去數寸，隅垂赤麻，餘與旌同。

translations.literal: The staff had three painted wooden disks suspended, several cun apart, corners hanging red hemp; the rest like the banner.
translations.idiomatic: The staff suspended three painted wooden disks several cun apart with red hemp at the corners; otherwise like the banner.

sentences.zh: 高宗給五品以上隨身魚銀袋，以防召命之詐，出內必合之。

translations.literal: Gaozong gave fifth rank and above silver personal-fish bags to guard against fraudulent summons; when leaving the palace they had to match.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong gave fifth rank and above silver personal-fish bags against fraudulent summons; they had to match when leaving the palace.

sentences.zh: 三品以上金飾袋。

translations.literal: Third rank and above had gold-ornament bags.
translations.idiomatic: Third rank and above used gold-ornament bags.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，都督、刺史始賜魚。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, military commissioners and prefects first received fish.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong reign period, military commissioners and prefects first received fish tokens.

sentences.zh: 天授二年，改佩魚皆為龜。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tian-shou, wearing fish was changed to wearing tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: In Tian-shou year 2 fish tokens became tortoise tokens.

sentences.zh: 其後三品以上龜袋飾以金，四品以銀，五品以銅。

translations.literal: Afterward third rank and above had tortoise bags ornamented with gold, fourth rank with silver, fifth rank with copper.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter third rank and above had gold-ornament tortoise bags, fourth silver, fifth copper.

sentences.zh: 中宗初，罷龜袋，復給以魚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongzong's reign tortoise bags were abolished and fish restored.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhongzong's accession tortoise bags were abolished and fish restored.

sentences.zh: 郡王、嗣王亦佩金魚袋。

translations.literal: Heir-presumptive princes and successor princes also wore gold fish bags.
translations.idiomatic: Heir-presumptive and successor princes also wore gold fish bags.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，令特進佩魚，散官佩魚自此始也。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era an edict ordered specially advanced officials to wear fish — fish for honorary officials began then.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinglong era specially advanced officials were ordered to wear fish—honorary officials' fish tokens began then.

sentences.zh: 然員外、試、檢校官，猶不佩魚。

translations.literal: Yet supernumerary, probationary, and acting officials still did not wear fish.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary, probationary, and acting officials still did not wear fish.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，詔衣紫者魚袋以金飾之，衣緋者以銀飾之。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era an edict ordered those wearing purple to have gold-ornament fish bags and those wearing deep red silver-ornament bags.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingyun era those in purple used gold-ornament fish bags and those in deep red silver-ornament bags.

sentences.zh: 開元初，駙馬都尉從五品者假紫、金魚袋，都督、刺史品卑者假緋、魚袋，五品以上檢校、試、判官皆佩魚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, consorts of the emperor's sons-in-law from fifth rank wore borrowed purple and gold fish bags; military commissioners and prefects of low rank borrowed deep red and fish bags; acting and probationary officials of fifth rank and above all wore fish.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiyuan saw fifth-rank consorts of sons-in-law in borrowed purple and gold fish bags, low-rank commissioners and prefects in borrowed deep red and fish, and fifth-rank acting and probationary officials all wearing fish.

sentences.zh: 中書令張嘉貞奏，致仕者佩魚終身，自是百官賞緋、紫，必兼魚袋，謂之章服。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zhang Jiazhen memorialized that retirees wore fish for life; thereafter officials rewarded with deep red or purple necessarily also received fish bags — called regalia dress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen memorialized that retirees kept fish for life; thereafter deep-red or purple rewards always included fish bags—regalia dress.

sentences.zh: 當時服朱紫、佩魚者眾矣。

translations.literal: At the time many wore vermilion, purple, and fish.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials then wore vermilion, purple, and fish.

sentences.zh: 初，隋文帝聽朝之服，以赭黃文綾袍，烏紗冒，折上巾，六合鞾，與貴臣通服。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wen of Sui's court dress was ochre-yellow patterned silk robe, black gauze cap, folded-up kerchief, and six-combination boots, shared with noble ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Emperor Wen of Sui wore an ochre-yellow patterned silk robe, black gauze cap, folded-up kerchief, and six-combination boots—the same as noble ministers.

sentences.zh: 唯天子之帶有十三鐶，文官又有平頭小樣巾，百官常服同於庶人。

translations.literal: Only the Son of Heaven's belt had thirteen rings; civil officials also had the flat small-pattern kerchief; officials' everyday dress was like commoners'.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Son of Heaven's belt had thirteen rings; civil officials had the flat small-pattern kerchief; everyday official dress matched commoners'.

sentences.zh: 至唐高祖，以赭黃袍、巾帶為常服。

translations.literal: When Tang Gaozu came, ochre-yellow robe and kerchief belt became everyday dress.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Gaozu the ochre-yellow robe and kerchief belt became everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 腰帶者，搢垂頭於下，名曰䤩尾，取順下之義。

translations.literal: For belts, the inserted end hung below, called "stepping on the tail," taking the meaning of following downward.
translations.idiomatic: Belt tabs hung below as a "stepping tail," signifying submission downward.

sentences.zh: 一品、二品銙以金，六品以上以犀，九品以上以銀，庶人以鐵。

translations.literal: First and second rank plaques of gold; sixth rank and above rhinoceros; ninth rank and above silver; commoners iron.
translations.idiomatic: First and second rank used gold belt plaques; sixth and above rhinoceros; ninth and above silver; commoners iron.

sentences.zh: 既而天子袍衫稍用赤、黃，遂禁臣民服。

translations.literal: Afterward the Son of Heaven's robe and jacket slightly used red and yellow, and subjects were forbidden to wear them.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor's robes used more red and yellow, and subjects were forbidden those hues.

sentences.zh: 親王及三品、二王後，服大科綾羅，色用紫，飾以玉。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and third rank, and consorts of second-rank princes, wore large-pattern silk gauze in purple, ornamented with jade.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes, third rank, and second-rank princes' consorts wore large-pattern silk gauze in purple with jade ornament.

sentences.zh: 五品以上服小科綾羅，色用朱，飾以金。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above wore small-pattern silk gauze in vermilion, ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above wore small-pattern silk gauze in vermilion with gold ornament.

sentences.zh: 六品以上服絲布交梭雙紃綾，色用黃。

translations.literal: Sixth rank and above wore cross-weave double-cord silk gauze in yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth rank and above wore cross-weave double-cord silk gauze in yellow.

sentences.zh: 六品、七品服用綠，飾以銀。

translations.literal: Sixth and seventh rank wore green, ornamented with silver.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth and seventh rank wore green with silver ornament.

sentences.zh: 八品、九品服用青，飾以鍮石。

translations.literal: Eighth and ninth rank wore azure, ornamented with copper-tin.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth and ninth rank wore azure with copper-tin ornament.

sentences.zh: 勳官之服，隨其品而加佩刀、礪、紛、帨。

translations.literal: Merit officials' dress followed their rank, adding worn sword, whetstone, fen, and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Merit officials dressed by rank, adding sword, whetstone, fen, and sash.

sentences.zh: 流外官、庶人、部曲、奴婢，則服紬絹絁布，色用黃白，飾以鐵、銅。

translations.literal: Outside-the-register officials, commoners, dependent households, and slaves wore coarse silk, ramie, and cloth in yellow-white, ornamented with iron and copper.
translations.idiomatic: Outside-register officials, commoners, dependents, and slaves wore coarse silk, ramie, and cloth in yellow-white with iron and copper ornament.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，又命七品服龜甲雙巨十花綾，色用綠。

translations.literal: In Taizong's time it was also ordered that seventh rank wear tortoise-armor double-giant ten-blossom silk gauze in green.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also ordered seventh rank to wear tortoise-armor double-giant ten-blossom silk gauze in green.

sentences.zh: 九品服絲布雜綾，色用青。

translations.literal: Ninth rank wore mixed-pattern silk cloth in azure.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth rank wore mixed-pattern silk cloth in azure.

sentences.zh: 是時士人以棠苧襴衫為上服，貴女功之始也。

translations.literal: At the time scholars took the tang ramie openwork shirt as upper dress, honoring the beginning of women's work.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars then favored the tang ramie openwork shirt as upper dress, honoring the origin of women's weaving.

sentences.zh: 一命以黃，再命以黑，三命以纁，四命以綠，五命以紫。

translations.literal: First appointment yellow, second black, third xuan, fourth green, fifth purple.
translations.idiomatic: Rank colors ran yellow for first appointment, black for second, xuan for third, green for fourth, purple for fifth.

sentences.zh: 士服短褐，庶人以白。

translations.literal: Scholars wore short brown; commoners white.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars wore short brown; commoners white.

sentences.zh: 中書令馬周上議：「禮無服衫之文，三代之制有深衣。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Ma Zhou memorialized: "Rites have no text on shirt dress; the three dynasties had deep robes.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou memorialized: "Ritual has no provision for shirt dress; the three dynasties used deep robes.

sentences.zh: 請加襴、袖、褾、襈，為士人上服。

translations.literal: Please add openwork, sleeves, cuffs, and placket as scholars' upper dress.
translations.idiomatic: Please add openwork, sleeves, cuffs, and placket as scholars' upper dress.

sentences.zh: 開骻者名曰缺骻衫，庶人服之。

translations.literal: Those with open fork are called open-fork shirts, for commoners' wear.
translations.idiomatic: Open-fork garments should be called open-fork shirts for commoners.

sentences.zh: 」又請：「裹頭者，左右各三襵，以象三才，重繫前脚，以象二儀。

translations.literal: " He also requested: "For wrapped headcloths, three folds left and right to symbolize the three powers, doubled and tied before the brow to symbolize the two principles.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested wrapped headcloths with three folds left and right for the three powers, doubled and tied at the brow for the two principles.

sentences.zh: 」詔皆從之。

translations.literal: " Edicts all followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The edicts approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 太尉長孫无忌又議：「服袍者下加襴，緋、紫、綠皆視其品，庶人以白。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji again proposed: "Those wearing robes should add openwork below; deep red, purple, and green all according to rank; commoners white.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji proposed: "Robe wearers should add openwork below; deep red, purple, and green by rank; commoners white.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗以幞頭起於後周，便武事者也。

translations.literal: Taizong once said the futou arose in Later Zhou for military convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong noted that the futou arose in Later Zhou for military convenience.

sentences.zh: 方天下偃兵，採古制為翼善冠，自服之。

translations.literal: When the realm lay at rest he took ancient models for the Beneficent Crown and wore it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire was at peace he modeled the Beneficent Crown on antiquity and wore it himself.

sentences.zh: 又製進德冠以賜貴臣，玉𤪌，制如弁服，以金飾梁，花趺，三品以上加金絡，五品以上附山雲。

translations.literal: He also made the Advance-in-Virtue Crown to bestow on noble ministers — jade tassels, made like bian dress, with gold-ornament ridge, floral base; third rank and above added gold net; fifth rank and above added mountain and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: He also created the Advance-in-Virtue Crown for noble ministers—jade tassels like bian dress, gold-ornament ridge and floral base; third rank and above added gold net; fifth and above mountain and cloud.

sentences.zh: 自是元日、冬至、朔、望視朝，服翼善冠，衣白練裙襦。

translations.literal: Thereafter on New Year, winter solstice, first and fifteenth for viewing court, he wore the Beneficent Crown with white practice skirt and jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter on New Year, winter solstice, and first- and fifteenth-day court he wore the Beneficent Crown with white practice skirt and jacket.

sentences.zh: 常服則有袴褶與平巾幘，通用翼善冠。

translations.literal: Everyday dress had trousers, pleated coat, and flat kerchief, universally with the Beneficent Crown.
translations.idiomatic: Everyday dress paired trousers, pleated coat, and flat kerchief with the Beneficent Crown.

sentences.zh: 進德冠制如幞頭，皇太子乘馬則服進德冠，九𤪌，加金飾，犀簪導，亦有絝褶，燕服用紫。

translations.literal: The Advance-in-Virtue Crown was made like the futou; the heir apparent when riding horses wore the Advance-in-Virtue Crown with nine tassels, added gold ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, also trousers and pleated coat; for banquets he used purple.
translations.idiomatic: The Advance-in-Virtue Crown resembled the futou; the heir apparent wore it for riding with nine tassels, gold ornament, rhinoceros hairpin guide, and trousers and pleated coat; banquets called for purple.

sentences.zh: 其後朔、望視朝，仍用弁服。

translations.literal: Afterward for first-and-fifteenth viewing court he still used bian dress.
translations.idiomatic: Later he still used bian dress for first- and fifteenth-day court.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，長孫无忌等曰：「武德初，撰衣服令，天子祀天地服大裘冕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, Zhangsun Wuji and others said: "In early Wude, when the Dress Code was drafted, the Son of Heaven sacrificed to Heaven and Earth in Great Fur miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing year 1 Zhangsun Wuji and others said: "In early Wude the Dress Code had the Son of Heaven sacrifice to Heaven and Earth in Great Fur miǎn.

sentences.zh: 桉周郊被衮以象天，戴冕藻十有二旒，與大裘異。

translations.literal: According to Zhou, at suburban sacrifice he wore gun to symbolize Heaven, miǎn with twelve tassel-threads of waterweed — differing from Great Fur.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou rites had suburban sacrifice in gun robe symbolizing Heaven and miǎn with twelve waterweed tassels—unlike Great Fur.

sentences.zh: 月令：孟冬，天子始裘以禦寒。

translations.literal: Monthly Ordinances: in mid-winter the Son of Heaven first donned fur to guard against cold.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances say mid-winter was when the Son of Heaven first donned fur against the cold.

sentences.zh: 若啟蟄祈穀、冬至報天，服裘可也。

translations.literal: If at the awakening of insects one prayed for grain or at the winter solstice reported to Heaven, wearing fur would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Fur would suit the insect-awakening grain prayer or winter-solstice heaven report.

sentences.zh: 季夏迎氣，龍見而雩，如之何可服？

translations.literal: But in late summer receiving the season, dragon appearance and rain prayer — how could one wear it?
translations.idiomatic: But late-summer season reception, dragon appearance, and rain prayer—how could fur be worn then?

sentences.zh: 故歷代唯服衮章。

translations.literal: Therefore successive ages wore only gun emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Hence successive ages wore only gun regalia.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝始采周官、禮記制祀天地之服，天子備十二章，後魏、周、隋皆如之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han first took Zhou offices and Rites to make dress for sacrificing to Heaven and Earth; the Son of Heaven had all twelve emblems; later Wei, Zhou, and Sui were alike.
translations.idiomatic: Han Emperor Ming first used Zhou offices and the Rites for Heaven-and-Earth sacrifice dress with twelve emblems; later Wei, Northern Zhou, and Sui followed.

sentences.zh: 伏請郊祀天地服衮冕，罷大裘。

translations.literal: We respectfully request that at suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth he wear gun miǎn and abolish Great Fur.
translations.idiomatic: We request suburban Heaven-and-Earth sacrifice in gun miǎn and abolition of Great Fur.

sentences.zh: 又新禮，皇帝祭社稷服絺冕，四旒，三章；

translations.literal: Also in the new rites, the emperor sacrificing to the altars of soil and grain wore xi miǎn with four tassels and three emblems;
translations.idiomatic: The new rites also had the emperor sacrifice to soil-and-grain altars in xi miǎn with four tassels and three emblems;

sentences.zh: 祭日月服玄冕，三旒，衣無章。

translations.literal: sacrificing to sun and moon wore xuan miǎn with three tassels and no emblems on the coat.
translations.idiomatic: sun and moon sacrifice in xuan miǎn with three tassels and no coat emblems.

sentences.zh: 按令文，四品、五品之服也。

translations.literal: According to the code text, that is fourth- and fifth-rank dress.
translations.idiomatic: By the code, those were fourth- and fifth-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 三公亞獻皆服衮，孤卿服毳、鷩，是天子同於大夫，君少臣多，非禮之中。

translations.literal: The three dukes as secondary offerers all wore gun; ministers and grand masters wore cui and bi — the Son of Heaven thus equaled grand masters, the lord fewer and ministers more, not the middle of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The three dukes as secondary offerers wore gun while ministers wore cui and bi—making the Son of Heaven equal to grand masters, contrary to proper hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 且天子十二為節以法天，烏有四旒三章之服？

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven's twelve sections symbolize Heaven — how could there be dress of four tassels and three sections?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's twelve sections symbolize Heaven—how could he wear four tassels and three sections?

sentences.zh: 若諸臣助祭，冕與王同，是貴賤無分也。

translations.literal: If assisting ministers' miǎn equaled the king's, noble and base were undivided.
translations.idiomatic: If assisting ministers' miǎn matched the king's, rank was undivided.

sentences.zh: 若降王一等，則王服玄冕，羣臣服爵弁，既屈天子，又貶公卿。

translations.literal: If the king were lowered one grade, then the king would wear xuan miǎn and the host of ministers jue bian — both humbling the Son of Heaven and demoting dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Lowering the king one grade would put xuan miǎn on the king and jue bian on ministers—humbling both throne and high ministers.

sentences.zh: 周禮此文，久不用矣，猶祭祀之有尸侑，以君親而拜臣子。

translations.literal: This Zhou-rites text has long gone unused, like still having corpse and surrogate in sacrifice — the lord bowing to his ministers as kin.
translations.idiomatic: That Zhou-rites text had long fallen out of use, like retaining corpse and surrogate rites where the lord bows to ministers as kin.

sentences.zh: 硩蔟、蟈氏之職，不通行者蓋多，故漢魏承用衮冕。

translations.literal: The duties of the reed-shield and frog-catcher offices, not practiced, were many; hence Han and Wei continued gun miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Many offices like reed-shield and frog-catcher were no longer practiced; Han and Wei therefore kept gun miǎn.

sentences.zh: 今新禮親祭日月，服五品之服，請循歷代故事，諸祭皆用衮冕。

translations.literal: Now the new rites have the emperor personally sacrifice to sun and moon in fifth-rank dress; we request following successive ages' precedent — all sacrifices use gun miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: The new rites had the emperor sacrifice to sun and moon in fifth-rank dress; we ask to follow precedent and use gun miǎn for all sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The decree said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The decree read: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」无忌等又曰：「禮，皇帝為諸臣及五服親舉哀，素服，今服白袷，禮令乖舛。

translations.literal: " Wuji and others also said: "By rites, when the emperor mourns for ministers and five-degree kin he wears plain dress; now he wears white lined coat — the code and rites conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji also said: "Rites required plain dress when the emperor mourned ministers and five-degree kin; the white lined coat conflicted with ritual.

sentences.zh: 且白袷出近代，不可用。

translations.literal: Moreover the white lined coat arose in recent times and cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: The white lined coat was a recent invention and should not be used.

sentences.zh: 」乃改以素服。

translations.literal: " Then plain dress was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: " Plain dress was adopted instead.

sentences.zh: 自是鷩冕以下，天子不復用，而白袷廢矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter from bi miǎn down the Son of Heaven no longer used them, and the white lined coat was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Son of Heaven abandoned bi miǎn and below, and the white lined coat was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其後以紫為三品之服，金玉帶銙十三；

translations.literal: Afterward purple became third-rank dress, with jade-gold belt and thirteen plaques;
translations.idiomatic: Later purple became third-rank dress with jade-gold belt of thirteen plaques;

sentences.zh: 緋為四品之服，金帶銙十一；

translations.literal: deep red fourth-rank dress, gold belt eleven plaques;
translations.idiomatic: deep red fourth-rank dress with gold belt of eleven plaques;

sentences.zh: 淺緋為五品之服，金帶銙十；

translations.literal: light deep red fifth-rank dress, gold belt ten plaques;
translations.idiomatic: light deep red fifth-rank dress with gold belt of ten plaques;

sentences.zh: 深綠為六品之服，淺綠為七品之服，皆銀帶銙九；

translations.literal: dark green sixth-rank, light green seventh-rank, both silver belt nine plaques;
translations.idiomatic: dark green sixth-rank and light green seventh-rank both used silver belts of nine plaques;

sentences.zh: 深青為八品之服，淺青為九品之服，皆鍮石帶銙八；

translations.literal: dark azure eighth-rank, light azure ninth-rank, both copper-tin belt eight plaques;
translations.idiomatic: dark azure eighth-rank and light azure ninth-rank both used copper-tin belts of eight plaques;

sentences.zh: 黃為流外官及庶人之服，銅鐵帶銙七。

translations.literal: yellow for outside-register officials and commoners, copper-iron belt seven plaques.
translations.idiomatic: yellow for outside-register officials and commoners with copper-iron belts of seven plaques.

sentences.zh: 武后擅政，多賜羣臣巾子、繡袍，勒以回文之銘，皆無法度，不足紀。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu usurped government she often bestowed on ministers kerchiefs and embroidered robes, compelled with turning-text inscriptions — all without law, not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu dominated government she often bestowed kerchiefs and embroidered robes inscribed with turning text—all outside the law and not worth recording.

sentences.zh: 至中宗又賜百官英王踣樣巾，其製高而踣，帝在藩時冠也。

translations.literal: Under Zhongzong she again bestowed on all officials the Prince of Ying stumbling-pattern kerchief, high and stumbling — what the emperor wore while in the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong bestowed on all officials the Prince of Ying stumbling-pattern kerchief—high and forward-leaning—the style he had worn as heir.

sentences.zh: 其後文官以紫黑絁為巾，賜供奉官及諸司長官；

translations.literal: Afterward civil officials used purple-black silk as kerchief, bestowed on palace attendants and bureau chiefs;
translations.idiomatic: Later civil officials used purple-black silk kerchiefs for palace attendants and bureau chiefs;

sentences.zh: 則有羅巾、圓頭巾子，後遂不改。

translations.literal: then there were gauze kerchiefs and round-top kerchiefs, unchanged thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: then gauze and round-top kerchiefs, unchanged thereafter.

sentences.zh: 初，職事官三品以上賜金裝刀、礪石，一品以下則有手巾、算袋、佩刀、礪石。

translations.literal: At first active officials of third rank and above were bestowed gold-fitted knives and whetstones; first rank and below had hand towels, tally bags, worn sword, and whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: Originally active third rank and above received gold-fitted knives and whetstones; first rank and below received hand towels, tally bags, swords, and whetstones.

sentences.zh: 至睿宗時，罷佩刀、礪石，而武官五品以上佩䪓韘七事，佩刀、刀子、礪石、契苾真、噦厥針筒、火石是也。

translations.literal: By Ruizong's time worn sword and whetstone were abolished, while military officials of fifth rank and above wore seven archer's-glove items: sword, knife, whetstone, qibi-zhen, wheezing needle tube, and fire stone.
translations.idiomatic: By Ruizong's reign worn swords and whetstones were abolished; fifth-rank military officials wore seven archer's-glove items—sword, knife, whetstone, qibi-zhen, wheezing needle tube, and fire stone.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子將釋奠，有司草儀注，從臣皆乘馬著衣冠，左庶子劉子玄議曰：「古大夫乘車，以馬為騑服，魏、晉朝士駕牛車。

translations.literal: At the time the heir apparent was about to perform the libation-of-paste; the relevant offices drafted ritual notes having followers all ride horses in cap and dress; Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Liu Zixuan proposed:
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was to perform the libation-of-paste, ritual drafters had followers ride horses in full cap and dress; Left Assistant Liu Zixuan objected:

sentences.zh: 如李廣北征，解鞍憩息；

translations.literal: Like Li Guang on the northern campaign, unstrapping the saddle to rest;
translations.idiomatic: as when Li Guang on the northern campaign unstrapped his saddle to rest;

sentences.zh: 馬援南伐，據鞍顧眄。

translations.literal: Ma Yuan on the southern campaign, sitting the saddle and looking back.
translations.idiomatic: as when Ma Yuan on the southern campaign sat his saddle and looked back.

sentences.zh: 則鞍馬行於軍旅，戎服所便。

translations.literal: Then saddle and horse go with the army — military dress is convenient for it.
translations.idiomatic: Saddle and horse belong to campaigns; military dress suits them.

sentences.zh: 江左尚書郎乘馬，則御史治之。

translations.literal: In the Jiangzuo era Secretariat directors riding horses were prosecuted by the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangzuo era Secretariat directors who rode horses were prosecuted by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 顏延年罷官，騎馬出入，世稱放誕。

translations.literal: Yan Yanzhi after leaving office rode horses in and out — the age called it unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yanzhi, dismissed from office, still rode in and out—the age called it unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 近古專車則衣朝服，單馬則衣褻服。

translations.literal: In recent antiquity exclusive carriage meant court dress; single horse meant informal dress.
translations.idiomatic: In recent antiquity a dedicated carriage meant court dress; a single horse meant informal dress.

sentences.zh: 皇家巡謁陵廟，冊命王公，則盛服冠履，乘路車。

translations.literal: The imperial house touring and worshiping tombs and investing princes and dukes wore full dress, cap, and shoes and rode the state chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tomb tours and investitures of princes and dukes required full dress, cap, shoes, and the state chariot.

sentences.zh: 士庶有以衣冠親迎者，亦時服箱。

translations.literal: Nobles and commoners who welcomed brides in cap and dress also used timely dress in the carriage box.
translations.idiomatic: When nobles and commoners welcomed brides in cap and dress they used timely dress from the carriage box.

sentences.zh: 其餘貴賤，皆以騎代車。

translations.literal: For the rest, noble and base all used riding in place of the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise all ranks rode horseback instead of chariots.

sentences.zh: 比者，法駕所幸，侍臣朝服乘馬。

translations.literal: Recently, where the imperial guard traveled, attending ministers wore court dress riding horses.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the imperial guard traveled, attending ministers wore court dress on horseback.

sentences.zh: 今既舍車，而冠履不易，何者？

translations.literal: Now having abandoned the chariot, yet cap and shoes are not changed — why?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the chariot is abandoned, why leave cap and shoes unchanged?

sentences.zh: 褒衣、博帶、革履、高冠，車中之服也。

translations.literal: Broad robes, wide belt, leather shoes, and high cap are dress for inside the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Broad robes, wide belt, leather shoes, and high cap are chariot dress.

sentences.zh: 韈而鐙，跣而乘，非唯盭古，亦自取驚蹶。

translations.literal: Socks on the stirrup, barefoot riding — not only overturning antiquity but also inviting falls.
translations.idiomatic: Riding in socks on the stirrup or barefoot overturns antiquity and invites falls.

sentences.zh: 議者以祕閣梁南郊圖，有衣冠乘馬者，此圖後人所為也。

translations.literal: Critics cited the Secret Archive's southern suburban painting with cap and dress on horseback — that painting was made by later men.
translations.idiomatic: Critics cited a Secret Archive southern-suburb painting of cap-and-dress horsemen—but that was a later painting.

sentences.zh: 古今圖畫多矣，如畫羣公祖二疏，而有曳芒屩者；

translations.literal: Ancient and modern paintings are many: painting the host of ministers seeing off the two Shus, yet some drag straw sandals;
translations.idiomatic: Paintings abound: one shows ministers seeing off the two Shus with figures in straw sandals;

sentences.zh: 畫昭君入匈奴，而婦人有施帷冒者。

translations.literal: painting Wang Zhaojun entering the Xiongnu, yet women wear draped veils.
translations.idiomatic: another shows Wang Zhaojun entering the Xiongnu with women in draped veils.

sentences.zh: 夫芒屩出於水鄉，非京華所有；

translations.literal: Straw sandals come from water districts, not the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Straw sandals belong to water districts, not the capital;

sentences.zh: 帷冒創於隋代，非漢宮所用。

translations.literal: draped veils were created in Sui times, not used in Han palaces.
translations.idiomatic: draped veils were a Sui invention, not Han palace dress.

sentences.zh: 豈可因二畫以為故實乎？

translations.literal: How can one take two paintings as established fact?
translations.idiomatic: Two paintings cannot establish ritual fact.

sentences.zh: 謂乘馬衣冠宜省。

translations.literal: They held that riding horses in cap and dress should be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that cap-and-dress horsemanship should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」太子從之，編於令。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent followed it and entered it in the code.
translations.idiomatic: " The heir apparent agreed and entered it in the code.

sentences.zh: 開元初，將有事南郊，中書令張說請遵古制用大裘，乃命有司製二冕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, when the southern suburb rite was planned, Secretariat Director Zhang Yue requested following ancient models to use Great Fur; the relevant offices were ordered to make two miǎn.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiyuan, planning the southern suburb, Zhang Yue requested Great Fur by ancient precedent and two miǎn were made.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以大裘樸略，不可通寒暑，廢而不服。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, because Great Fur was plain and rough and could not pass through cold and heat, abolished it and did not wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong found Great Fur too plain for seasonal use and never wore it.

sentences.zh: 自是元正朝會用衮冕、通天冠，百官朔、望朝參，外官衙日，則佩算袋，餘日則否。

translations.literal: Thereafter New Year court used gun miǎn and Pervading Heaven Crown; officials attended first-and-fifteenth court; outside officials on yamen days wore tally bags, not on other days.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter New Year court used gun miǎn and Pervading Heaven Crown; officials on first-and-fifteenth court; outside officials wore tally bags only on yamen days.

sentences.zh: 玄宗謁五陵，初用素服，朔、望朝顓用常服。

translations.literal: Xuanzong worshiped the five tombs, at first using plain dress; first-and-fifteenth court and audiences used everyday dress.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong at first used plain dress for the five tombs; first-and-fifteenth audiences used everyday dress.

sentences.zh: 弁服、翼善冠皆廢。

translations.literal: Bian dress and Beneficent Crown were both abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Bian dress and the Beneficent Crown were abolished.

sentences.zh: 唐初，賞朱紫者服於軍中，其後軍將亦賞以假緋紫，有從戎缺骻之服，不在軍者服長袍，或無官而冒衣綠。

translations.literal: Early Tang rewarded vermilion and purple for wear in the army; afterward military commanders were also rewarded with borrowed deep red and purple; there was campaign open-fork dress; those not in the army wore long robes, and some without office falsely wore green.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang rewarded vermilion and purple for army wear; later commanders received borrowed deep red and purple; campaign open-fork dress existed; off-duty men wore long robes and some without rank wore green falsely.

sentences.zh: 有詔殿中侍御史糾察。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Palace Attendant censors to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Palace Attendant censors to investigate.

sentences.zh: 諸衞大將軍、中郎將以下給袍者，皆易其繡文：千牛衞以瑞牛，左右衞以瑞馬，驍衞以虎，武衞以鷹，威衞以豹，領軍衞以白澤，金吾衞以辟邪。

translations.literal: For palace guards from Great General and Colonel down who received robes, the embroidery was changed: Thousand-Ox Guard auspicious ox, Left and Right Guards auspicious horse, Valiant Cavalry tiger, Martial Guard eagle, Awesome Guard leopard, Army-leader Guard white ze, Gold Crow Guard demon-warder.
translations.idiomatic: Guard units from Great General down had distinct robe embroidery: Thousand-Ox auspicious ox, Left and Right Guards auspicious horse, Valiant Cavalry tiger, Martial Guard eagle, Awesome Guard leopard, Army-leader white ze, Gold Crow demon-warder.

sentences.zh: 行六品者，冠去𤪌珠，五品去鞶囊、雙佩，幞頭用羅縠。

translations.literal: Sixth-rank campaigners removed tassel pearls from the crown; fifth rank removed pan bag and double pendant; futou used gauze damask.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth-rank campaigners removed crown tassel pearls; fifth rank removed pan bag and double pendant; futou used gauze damask.

sentences.zh: 婦人服從夫、子，五等以上親及五品以上母、妻，服紫衣，腰襻褾緣用錦繡。

translations.literal: Women's dress followed husband and son; kin of fifth rank and above and mothers and wives of fifth rank and above wore purple, waist sash, cuffs, and borders in brocade embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Women dressed by husband and son; fifth-rank kin and fifth-rank mothers and wives wore purple with brocade-embroidered waist sash, cuffs, and borders.

sentences.zh: 九品以上母、妻，服朱衣。

translations.literal: Mothers and wives of ninth rank and above wore vermilion.
translations.idiomatic: Mothers and wives of ninth rank and above wore vermilion.

sentences.zh: 流外及庶人不服綾、羅、縠、五色線鞾、履。

translations.literal: Outside-register persons and commoners did not wear damask, gauze, openwork, five-color thread boots, or shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Outside-register persons and commoners could not wear damask, gauze, openwork, five-color thread boots, or shoes.

sentences.zh: 凡襇色衣不過十二破，渾色衣不過六破。

translations.literal: For patterned-color dress, not more than twelve sections; for solid-color dress, not more than six sections.
translations.idiomatic: Patterned dress was limited to twelve sections; solid-color dress to six.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，御史大夫李適之建議：「冬至、元日大禮，朝參官及六品清官服朱衣，六品以下通服絝褶。

translations.literal: In year twenty-five, Censor-in-chief Li Shizhi proposed: "For winter solstice and New Year great rites, attending officials and sixth-rank pure officials wear vermilion; sixth rank and below universally wear trousers and pleated coat.
translations.idiomatic: In year 25 Li Shizhi proposed that winter-solstice and New Year great rites have attending and sixth-rank pure officials in vermilion while sixth rank and below wore trousers and pleated coat.

sentences.zh: 」天寶中，御史中丞吉溫建議：「京官朔、望朝參，衣朱絝褶，五品以上有珂傘。

translations.literal: " In the Tianbao era, Vice Censor-in-chief Ji Wen proposed: "Capital officials on first-and-fifteenth court wear vermilion trousers and pleated coat; fifth rank and above have ke umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Tianbao era Ji Wen proposed capital officials in vermilion trousers and pleated coat on first-and-fifteenth court, fifth rank and above with ke umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 」德宗嘗賜節度使時服，以鵰銜綬帶，謂其行列有序，牧人有威儀也。

translations.literal: Dezong once bestowed seasonal dress on military commissioners with eagle-holding-sash belt, saying their ranks were ordered and shepherds had dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong once bestowed seasonal dress on commissioners with eagle-holding-sash belts, saying ordered ranks gave shepherds dignity.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，太子少師鄭餘慶言：「百官服朝服者多誤。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent Zheng Yuyu said: "Many officials err in court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe year 12 Zheng Yuyu said many officials erred in court dress.

sentences.zh: 自今唯職事官五品兼六品以上散官者，則有佩、劍、綬，其餘皆省。

translations.literal: From now only active officials of fifth rank and honorary sixth rank and above have pendant, sword, and sash; the rest are reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only active fifth rank and honorary sixth rank and above would keep pendant, sword, and sash; others would not.

sentences.zh: 初，婦人施羃䍦以蔽身，永徽中，始用帷冒，施裙及頸，坐檐以代乘車。

translations.literal: At first women wore face-covering veil to screen the body; in the Yonghui era they first used draped veil with skirt to the neck, sitting canopy in place of riding in a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Women first used face-covering veils; in Yonghui they adopted draped veils with skirt to the neck and sedan canopies instead of carriages.

sentences.zh: 命婦朝謁，則以駝駕車。

translations.literal: Wives by grant attending court used camel-drawn carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Granted wives at court used camel-drawn carriages.

sentences.zh: 數下詔禁而不止。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts forbade it but it did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated edicts failed to stop the practice.

sentences.zh: 武后時，帷冒益盛，中宗後乃無復羃䍦矣。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu draped veils grew more common; after Zhongzong the face-covering veil was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu draped veils spread; after Zhongzong the old face veil disappeared.

sentences.zh: 宮人從駕，皆胡冒乘馬，海內傚之，至露髻馳騁，而帷冒亦廢，有衣男子衣而鞾，如奚、契丹之服。

translations.literal: Palace women following the guard all wore Hu veils on horseback; the realm imitated them until they rode with hair exposed; veils were abandoned and some women wore men's clothes and boots like Xi and Khitan dress.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women on guard wore Hu veils on horseback; the realm imitated them until hair was exposed in riding; veils vanished and some women wore men's clothes and boots like Xi and Khitan dress.

sentences.zh: 武德間，婦人曳履及線鞾。

translations.literal: In the Wude era women dragged shoes and thread boots.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era women dragged shoes and thread boots.

sentences.zh: 開元中，初有線鞋，侍兒則著履，奴婢服襴衫，而士女衣胡服，其後安祿山反，當時以為服妖之應。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan thread shoes first appeared; attendants wore slippers, slave girls wore openwork shirts, while gentlemen and ladies wore Hu dress — after An Lushan's rebellion it was taken as an omen of dress perversion.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiyuan introduced thread shoes; attendants wore slippers, maids openwork shirts, and gentlemen and ladies Hu dress—after An Lushan's rebellion deemed a dress omen.

sentences.zh: 巴、蜀婦人出入有兜籠，乾元初，蕃將又以兜籠易負，遂以代車。

translations.literal: Ba and Shu women going out had carrying baskets; in the early Qianyuan era frontier generals also replaced carrying on the back with baskets, thus replacing the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ba-Shu women used carrying baskets; early Qianyuan frontier generals replaced back-carrying with baskets, replacing carriages.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，以四方車服僭奢，下詔準儀制令，品秩勳勞為等級。

translations.literal: When Wenzong took the throne, because carriage and dress in the four quarters were presumptuous and extravagant, an edict followed the code of ritual regulations, with rank, merit, and labor as grades.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, finding regional carriage and dress presumptuous, ordered compliance with the ritual code graded by rank, merit, and service.

sentences.zh: 職事官服綠、青、碧，勳官諸司則佩刀、礪、紛、帨。

translations.literal: Active officials wore green, azure, and blue-green; merit offices of various bureaus wore sword, whetstone, fen, and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Active officials wore green, azure, and blue-green; merit offices wore sword, whetstone, fen, and sash.

sentences.zh: 諸親朝賀宴會之服：一品、二品服玉及通犀，三品服花犀、班犀。

translations.literal: Dress for imperial kin at congratulations and banquets: first and second rank jade and clear rhinoceros; third rank patterned rhinoceros and rimmed rhinoceros.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kin at congratulations and banquets: first and second rank jade and clear rhinoceros; third rank patterned and rimmed rhinoceros.

sentences.zh: 車馬無飾金銀。

translations.literal: Carriages and horses without gold or silver ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and horses bore no gold or silver ornament.

sentences.zh: 衣曳地不過二寸，袖不過一尺三寸。

translations.literal: Coat hems not more than two cun trailing; sleeves not more than one chi three cun.
translations.idiomatic: Coat hems trailed no more than two cun; sleeves no more than one chi three cun.

sentences.zh: 婦人裙不過五幅，曳地不過三寸，襦袖不過一尺五寸。

translations.literal: Women's skirts not more than five panels, hem not more than three cun trailing; jacket sleeves not more than one chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: Women's skirts had no more than five panels and three cun hem; jacket sleeves no more than one chi five cun.

sentences.zh: 袍襖之制：三品以上服綾，以鶻銜瑞草，鴈銜綬帶及雙孔雀；

translations.literal: Regulations for robes and jackets: third rank and above wore damask with hawk holding auspicious grass, goose holding sash, and paired peacocks;
translations.idiomatic: Robes and jackets: third rank and above wore damask with hawk holding auspicious grass, goose holding sash, and paired peacocks;

sentences.zh: 四品、五品服綾，以地黃交枝；

translations.literal: fourth and fifth rank damask with earth-yellow interlaced branches;
translations.idiomatic: fourth and fifth rank damask with earth-yellow interlaced branches;

sentences.zh: 六品以下服綾，小窠無文及隔織、獨織。

translations.literal: sixth rank and below small-nest damask without pattern, or spaced weave, or single weave.
translations.idiomatic: sixth and below small-nest plain damask, spaced weave, or single weave.

sentences.zh: 一品導從以七騎；

translations.literal: First rank had seven outriders in escort;
translations.idiomatic: First rank: seven escort riders;

sentences.zh: 二品、三品以五騎；

translations.literal: second and third rank five;
translations.idiomatic: second and third: five;

sentences.zh: 四品以三騎；

translations.literal: fourth rank three;
translations.idiomatic: fourth: three;

sentences.zh: 五品以二騎；

translations.literal: fifth rank two;
translations.idiomatic: fifth: two;

sentences.zh: 六品以一騎。

translations.literal: sixth rank one.
translations.idiomatic: sixth: one.

sentences.zh: 五品以上及節度使冊拜、婚會，則車有幰。

translations.literal: Fifth rank and above and military commissioners at investiture and wedding might have carriages with screens.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth rank and above and commissioners at investiture or wedding might use screened carriages.

sentences.zh: 外命婦一品、二品、三品乘金銅飾犢車，檐舁以八人，三品舁以六人；

translations.literal: Outside-title wives of first, second, and third rank rode gold-and-copper-ornament calf carts, canopy carried by eight men; third rank by six;
translations.idiomatic: Outside-title wives of first through third rank rode gold-and-copper calf carts—eight bearers for first and second, six for third;

sentences.zh: 四品、五品乘白銅飾犢車，檐舁以四人；

translations.literal: fourth and fifth rank white-copper calf carts, canopy carried by four;
translations.idiomatic: fourth and fifth white-copper calf carts with four bearers;

sentences.zh: 胥吏、商賈之妻老者乘葦軬車，兜籠舁以二人。

translations.literal: clerks' and merchants' elderly wives reed-canopy carts, basket carried by two.
translations.idiomatic: clerks' and merchants' elderly wives reed-canopy carts with two basket bearers.

sentences.zh: 度支、戶部、鹽鐵門官等服細葛布，無紋綾，綠闇銀藍鐵帶，鞍、轡、銜、鐙以鍮石。

translations.literal: Revenue, census, and salt-iron gate officers wore fine ramie cloth without patterned damask, green dark silver-blue iron belt, saddle, bridle, bit, and stirrup of copper-tin.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue, census, and salt-iron gate officers wore fine ramie without patterned damask, green dark silver-blue iron belts, and copper-tin saddle fittings.

sentences.zh: 未有官者，服粗葛布、官絁，綠銅鐵帶，乘蜀馬、鐵鐙。

translations.literal: Those without office wore coarse ramie and official silk, green copper-iron belt, Shu horses and iron stirrups.
translations.idiomatic: The unappointed wore coarse ramie and official silk, green copper-iron belts, Shu horses, and iron stirrups.

sentences.zh: 行官服紫粗布、絁，藍鐵帶。

translations.literal: Traveling officers wore purple coarse cloth and silk with blue iron belt.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling officers wore purple coarse cloth and silk with blue iron belts.

sentences.zh: 中官不衣紗縠綾羅，諸司小兒不服大巾，商賈、庶人、僧、道士不乘馬。

translations.literal: Palace eunuchs did not wear gauze damask or silk gauze; bureau boys did not wear large kerchiefs; merchants, commoners, monks, and Daoists did not ride horses.
translations.idiomatic: Palace eunuchs avoided gauze damask and silk gauze; bureau boys avoided large kerchiefs; merchants, commoners, monks, and Daoists did not ride horses.

sentences.zh: 婦人衣青碧纈、平頭小花草履、彩帛縵成履，而禁高髻、險妝、去眉、開額及吳越高頭草履。

translations.literal: Women's dress forbade azure-green tie-dye, flat small-flower grass shoes, and colored-silk woven shoes, while banning high topknots, extreme makeup, shaved brows, open forehead, and Wu-Yue high-head straw shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Women were barred from azure-green tie-dye, flat flower-grass shoes, and colored woven shoes, and from high topknots, extreme makeup, shaved brows, open foreheads, and Wu-Yue high-head straw shoes.

sentences.zh: 王公之居，不施重栱、藻井。

translations.literal: Princes' and dukes' residences did not use heavy bracketing or painted well ceilings.
translations.idiomatic: Princely and ducal residences could not use heavy bracketing or painted well ceilings.

sentences.zh: 三品堂五間九架，門三間五架；

translations.literal: Third rank: hall five bays nine frames, gate three bays five frames;
translations.idiomatic: Third rank: five-bay nine-frame hall, three-bay five-frame gate;

sentences.zh: 五品堂五間七架，門三間兩架；

translations.literal: fifth rank: hall five bays seven frames, gate three bays two frames;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank: five-bay seven-frame hall, three-bay two-frame gate;

sentences.zh: 六品、七品堂三間五架，庶人四架，而門皆一間兩架。

translations.literal: sixth and seventh rank: hall three bays five frames; commoners four frames, all gates one bay two frames.
translations.idiomatic: sixth and seventh: three-bay five-frame hall; commoners four frames; all gates one bay two frames.

sentences.zh: 常參官施懸魚、對鳳、瓦獸、通栿乳梁。

translations.literal: Regular-attendance officials might use suspended fish, facing phoenixes, tile beasts, and through-rafter nipple beams.
translations.idiomatic: Regular-attendance officials might use suspended fish, facing phoenixes, tile beasts, and through-rafter nipple beams.

sentences.zh: 詔下，人多怨者。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, many complained.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict issued, many complained.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰條易行者為寬限，而事遂不行。

translations.literal: Capital Intendant Du Cong listed what was easy to execute as a broad limit, and the matter then did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Capital Intendant Du Cong listed easy provisions as broad limits, and the reform failed.

sentences.zh: 唯淮南觀察使李德裕令管內婦人衣袖四尺者闊一尺五寸，裙曳地四五寸者減三寸。

translations.literal: Only Huainan Observation Commissioner Li Deyu ordered women within his circuit with sleeves four chi to narrow one chi five cun and skirts trailing four or five cun to shorten three cun.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Deyu in Huainan ordered women's four-chi sleeves narrowed to one chi five cun and skirts trailing four or five cun shortened three cun.

sentences.zh: 開成末，定制：宰相、三公、師保、尚書令、僕射、諸司長官及致仕官，疾病許乘檐，如漢、魏載輿、步輿之制，三品以上官及刺史，有疾暫乘，不得舍驛。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaicheng a fixed regulation: chancellors, three dukes, tutors, protectors, Secretariat Directors, Vice Directors, bureau chiefs, and retired officials when ill might ride sedan — like Han and Wei carrying litters and step litters; third rank and above and prefects might ride temporarily when ill but not lodge at stations.
translations.idiomatic: Late Kaicheng fixed rules: chancellors, three dukes, tutors, protectors, Secretariat Directors, Vice Directors, bureau chiefs, and retirees when ill might use sedans like Han-Wei litters; third rank and above and prefects might ride temporarily when ill but not lodge at postal stations.
